_spec.purpose: The automation-change trail. Every machine upgrade a run makes to itself.
_spec.why: A routine whose last phase edits its own machine will drift, and the drift is invisible unless each change is written down where the next run and the maintainer both see it. Each set reverts as one commit.
_spec.bound_by: ownership.yaml. An upgrade needing another actor's files is not an upgrade this run gets to make; it is written here as a proposal and stops.

_shape.discovered: 2026-08-18, by the first phase that ever tried to write this file
_shape.why_entries_is_empty: The `entries` array above is empty and will stay empty. ownership.yaml marks this path append_only, and ownership_check implements that as 'the diff contains no removed line'. Adding the first element to a JSON array moves its closing bracket, which rewrites the line `"entries": []`, so the array could never receive an entry and the rule refused the operation it exists to permit. Nothing had ever written this file, so nothing had ever found out.
_shape.how_to_append: One top level key per run date, with the COMMA LEADING on its own line, inserted immediately before the final closing brace. That is the only JSON shape that grows by pure insertion: the previous entry's closing brace is untouched because its separator lives on the next line, and the file's last line never moves. Read it with json.load and take every key that parses as a date.
_shape.the_rule_was_not_loosened: ownership.yaml was not edited and could not be: it belongs to the human actor. The shape moved to fit the rule rather than the rule moving to fit the shape.

upgrades.what: qa.py FAILS a non-decorative text line whose glyph band is crossed by a drawn rule, judged from new per-element geometry emitted by render.py
upgrades.why: slide 09 shipped with the field table's 2px `tr.last td` bottom rule at y=1215 running through the footnote's first line box [84,1204,691,31], and machine QA reported PASS with zero fails and zero warns. text_collisions compares TEXT to TEXT. The occlusion probe compares text to OPAQUE ELEMENT BOXES four or more px in both dimensions, and this rule painted BENEATH the footnote anyway. glyph_ink_contamination fires on ink of the glyphs' OWN value and the rule was a different colour on the same sheet. busy_art_under_text measures edge DENSITY, and one clean rule through a line is the lowest density structure there is. Every gate answered its own question correctly. The scorer found it by reading render_report.json's coordinates by hand at the ship gate, where a repair costs a rebuild.

every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.the glyph band: the em box centred in the measured line box, which is CSS's own content area for an inline box. Derived from the node's own font-size and its rendered line box, so nothing is typed and it scales with the type. Half leading falls outside it, which is what separates a rule THROUGH a word from a rule sitting in the gap under it.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.rule or plate: the strip's thickness must be under one em of the struck type. At one em or more the thing is a plate and the occlusion probe already owns plates. One em is the type's own unit.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.how much crossed: a horizontal rule must cross at least one em of the line, so a clipped corner is not a strike. A vertical rule must stand at least one em inside both ends of the line box, because a column divider brushing the end of a line box is ordinary and a vertical rule inside a run of words is not.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.can a reader see it: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11's 3.0:1 non-text contrast floor, MEASURED off the PNG between the strip's worst scan line and the paper beside it. An external published standard, so it cannot ratchet the way a figure derived from our own corpus would. Under it the strip is the quiet divider GATE_LESSONS 7 says is allowed to be quiet, and this gate says nothing about it.
every_quantity_and_where_it_came_from.paint order: deliberately not consulted, and that is not an oversight. The rule that shipped painted under the footnote and read as a strikethrough regardless.

upgrades.verification: python3 .claude/skills/carousel-engine/qa.py --self-test, 13 cases over THREE REAL CHROMIUM RENDERS of slide-09.html, cropped and re-based, because GATE_LESSONS 15 says a fixture written by the detector's author agrees with the detector. The pre-repair slide was reconstructed from score.json's recorded repair (table bottom 132px, footnote bottom 84px), re-rendered, and reproduced the scorer's exact numbers: minutes row 1155..1218, footnote line box [84,1204,691,31]. Case 2 is the deck AS SHIPPED and must be clean. Case 3 holds the geometry identical and swaps the 2px near-black rule for the table's own 1px rgba(95,115,80,0.45) hairline, so only the WCAG floor separates it from the defect. Case 7 runs the real entry point end to end through argparse and asserts exit 1: the first draft of that case grepped the source for a call to rule_strikes and stayed GREEN when the call was neutered to `[] and rule_strikes(...)`, which is GATE_LESSONS 13 reproduced inside the fix for something else. Four mutants were watched go red: the WCAG floor set to 0.0, the band widened to the whole line box, the thickness test loosened, and the call unwired. Separately, qa.py --render-dir over a fresh render of the shipped nine slide deck reports clean, so the check is not too blunt for slide 7's ruled empty box, slide 9's bounded empty fields or slide 5's labels above tiles.
upgrades.revert: this commit. render.py's `out.rules` block and qa.py's rule_strikes / strip_visibility / _text_mask are self contained, and the call site is four lines.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: a run reports a strike on a design where the rule is MEANT to touch the type, a fieldset legend sitting on its own border or a word set deliberately struck out. The escape hatch is data-overlap-ok, which demotes it to a WARN, and a second sighting would mean the em box band is the wrong shape rather than the floor being wrong. The opposite tell is silence: if a strikethrough ships again while this reports clean, the cause is a mark this probe does not emit, which today is canvas ink (owned by glyph_ink_contamination), an SVG <path>, or a diagonal line.

upgrades.what: claims_check.py owns the fact-checker's schema as well as the check. A --template flag prints a valid skeleton built from the file's own constants, and --self-test runs check() over the JSON example in the agent's spec and asserts that spec names every required field and every source type.
upgrades.why: the fact-checker's output was rejected on four separate field names in one run: source_url for url, journalism for secondary_reported, dropped for rejected, and no retrieved at all. The showrunner repaired it by hand across four round trips. The gate was right every time. The AGENT was guessing, because its only schema was a worked example carrying "url": "the page you fetched", which would itself have failed the gate, and because the four value source taxonomy appeared nowhere in the spec it reads. The sibling's recorded cost for this class of drift is an empty verification record on 14 of 18 decks.
upgrades.verification: python3 scripts/carousel/claims_check.py --self-test. Four new cases replay the 2026-08-18 output field by field. Three assert the spec check itself can go red: a spec with the taxonomy renamed to journalism is CAUGHT, a spec whose example uses source_url is CAUGHT, and the template this file prints must pass this file's own check. Nothing in the gate's strictness was relaxed and every sibling drift case still fails.
upgrades.revert: this commit. template(), spec_problems() and the --template flag are additive, and the agent spec change is a documentation edit.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: the spec check goes red on a spec edit that is actually an improvement, which would mean it is asserting prose rather than schema. It only requires each field name in backticks and each source type as a literal, so a rewrite that keeps the table keeps passing. If a future run still guesses a field name with all of this in place, the fix is not more documentation, it is piping --template into the agent's prompt, which is a proposal below.

upgrades.what: aggregate_check.py gains a third declaration route, `quoted_from` with `quote`, for a figure the SOURCE wrote rather than one the deck computed, and refuses a `computed_by` that describes quoting
upgrades.why: run No.2 had five quoted figures (two schools, four hours, 110 minutes, three blocks) and two routes to declare them. The count rule wants one claim id per unit counted, so 'two schools' would have had to name two claims, which is a lie in the shape that rule expects. So all five went through `computed_by`, a field whose name asserts the opposite of what happened and whose only check is that the prose runs to three words. The honest route was the unchecked one, and the aggregates file's _note carried the whole burden of explaining it.
upgrades.this_is_a_tightening_not_a_loosening: quoted_from verifies that the declared string actually occurs in the named claim and that the declared value is a numeral inside that string. Under computed_by, a quoted figure the source does not contain passed on a sentence nobody read.
upgrades.verification: python3 scripts/carousel/aggregate_check.py --self-test, seven new cases including four abuse paths (a quote the claim does not contain, a value that is not the number the source wrote, a claim id that does not exist, a claim id with no quote) and the 2026-08-18 workaround declaration word for word, which must now fail and must name the route that replaces it. Verified against REAL DATA as well: the shipped out/2026-08-18/aggregates.json now fails on four declarations, and rewriting those four to quoted_from against the run's real claims.json passes clean.
upgrades.revert: this commit. _rederive_quoted() and one branch at the top of rederive().
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: a run finds a legitimate computed_by refused because its prose happens to contain the words 'quoted from'. The pattern is narrow and a self-test case proves an honest computed_by mentioning quoted names still passes, but a second false refusal would mean the check should read the field's structure rather than its wording.

found_while_logging_this.what: ledger/carousel/upgrades.json could not receive its first entry
found_while_logging_this.detail: ownership.yaml marks this path append_only and ownership_check implements that as 'no removed line in the diff'. 2026-08-25.note:
26 machine changes across ten scoring rounds, far over the three the 2026-08-21 set called a ceiling, and the ceiling is not being quietly raised. Every one is a gate or an engine that was WRONG about the product rather than one that could be better, and all but two were found by a scoring panel or by another gate rather than by this phase going looking for work. A gate reporting clean over a defect is not a backlog item.

The round 9 panel is worth recording as a measurement of the panel itself. Three judges read independently and returned 6.0, 6.2 and 6.0 on `artwork_craft`, the heaviest criterion in the rubric, and all three named the same cause in their own words: the type layer did not know where the paper ended. One of them called it out on four frames. Machine QA had been reporting the worst instance for two rounds as "art touching glyphs", and the run read that as an atmosphere note both times. A single grader cannot produce that signal. Agreement across three is the only thing that separates a finding from a taste.

That is the reason it needs a gate rather than more care: a figure cannot reach a frame without passing compute.quoted(), and a locator reaches a frame by being typed into slide HTML with nothing in between. numeral_lint reads published site copy, not slide strings. copy_sync_check asks whether copy.json and the render agree, which they did. upgrades.the_design_note_that_cost_the_most: IT READS THE RENDER, NEVER copy.json. upgrades.the_carrier_set_and_the_judgement_made_o: quote and source_title. Requiring `quote` ALONE was considered and rejected BY MEASUREMENT: a locator names where in a document a sentence sits, so it is almost never inside the sentence, and eight of the thirteen are carried by source_title and nothing else. upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If it starts firing on a correct frame more often than on an uncarried locator. upgrades.what: panel.py can now tell a threshold dissent from a named fault, and fails closed on silence. A judge that sets ship:false with an empty hard_fails list must say `refusal_reason: threshold` to have its no read as a disagreement about the number.
upgrades.why: panel.py synthesised a hard fail whenever a judge returned ship:false with no hard fail named. That is right about the case it was written for and it fired twice on this deck for a different case. In round 4 the craft judge returned 6.684 and wrote 'the refusal is the threshold, not a fault'. In the final pass the integrity judge returned 6.51 with an empty list and wrote 'I looked hard for one and I will not manufacture it'. The rubric defines a hard fail as a claim about a promise this product made in public, and a threshold dissent is not one. A hard fail stops a deck at ANY round, so the run reached the cap reading its own gate as saying both ship and do not ship, and resolved it in four paragraphs of the run record. The cap is the one rule in this rubric that exists to end a loop and it was the one rule the tooling could not express.
upgrades.where_a_declared_dissent_goes: Into the SCORE, where it already is, and not into a veto beside it. This module's doctrine is median for numbers and union for faults, and a judge saying 'under the bar' has said it once already by scoring 6.51. Counting it in the median AND as a stop is one objection counted twice, which is how the gate ended up contradicting itself. That is simpler than the proposal's cap-conditional version and needs no round count.
three_things_still_fail_closed: silence. No refusal_reason at all is a fault refusal and stops the deck, which is the original rule unchanged.
any other word. A reason this panel does not recognise is a fault refusal, so a judge cannot invent a word to get past it.
an incoherent one. A judge claiming its no is about the number, while its own score clears the bar, has not described its own refusal.
upgrades.why_this_is_not_a_loosening_and_the_proo: It did not make this run pass and could not have. runs/carousel/2026-08-28/score.json was written during the run and already carries the synthesized entry, so shipped_check's completion gate is still red on that deck after this change, exactly as it was before it. The change is forward-looking, and score.json is the daily lane's file, not this one's. It also ADDS a requirement rather than removing one: a judge must now make an affirmative declaration to get the softer reading, and everything that stopped a deck before still stops it.
upgrades.verification: python3 scripts/carousel/panel.py --self-test, by exit code. Thirteen new assertions. Replayed against the defect in BOTH directions: forcing the pre-2026-08-28 behaviour (always synthesize) turns four of them red, and forcing the widening (treat every silent refusal as a dissent) turns three red including 'a judge returning ship:false with no hard fail still stops the deck'. The contract is published in config/carousel/scoring_rubric.yaml where the judges read it, and the self-test parses that file and asserts it names the same field and the same value the module reads, so the two spellings cannot drift.
upgrades.revert: revert the refusal block in panel.py combine() and the `refusal:` block in scoring_rubric.yaml
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If `refusal_reason: threshold` starts appearing on refusals that were actually about a fault the judge could not be bothered to write down. The signal is a run shipping over the bar with a dissent recorded and a later reader finding a real defect the dissenting judge had seen. If that happens the fix is to require the dissent to name the criterion it is under the bar on, not to delete the field, because deleting it puts the cap back in the state where it cannot fire.

upgrades.what: panel.py derives the kind of a refusal from the judge's own numbers and reads no declared field.
upgrades.why: The first version of this, shipped earlier the same day, read a `refusal_reason` field off the judge. The hole opened inside that same run: the integrity judge scored 6.51 and explained itself in prose, the field did not exist when it scored, and THE RUN WROTE THE FIELD ONTO THE JUDGE'S FILE. The panel moved from HOLD to SHIP on a word the graded party had typed. The run labelled it honestly in a key beside it, and honest labelling is not a control. A gate whose input the graded party can author is a formality with a good comment on it.
upgrades.how: The `s < bar` half of the old test was already derived and carried the whole meaning. A judge that returns ship:false, names no fault and scores under the bar has described a threshold dissent because there is nothing else it can be: the rubric gives a fault its own list and this judge left it empty. So the word is gone and there is nothing to transcribe. A written refusal_reason the judge's own numbers do not support now fails closed.

not_reached_and_why.proposal_11, a relationship between sour: This was ranked second by the phase that launched me and I did not build it, because I could not build a version I could demonstrate failing. The defect is exact: slide 6 printed `260 MW load + 265.5 MW generation`, guarded by an assertion in compute.py that the components equal the quoted 525.5. Every gate passed and the sentence was false, because the order's recital adds two LOADS and the 265.5 in that total is the Crusoe One Load as the applicants characterise it, not GOODNIT1's generation. A tautology cannot fail, so it certifies nothing. The proposed cure is a related(cid, ...) in compute.py that asks a claim rather than asking arithmetic. THE REASON IT IS STILL A PROPOSAL: compute.py is written fresh by the model every run and has no template file in any lane, so there is nowhere in scripts/ or .claude/ to put related(). The one seat that exists is aggregates.json, whose declaration format already carries quoted_from and from_claims, and a `kind: relation` entry requiring a claim id whose quote states the relation would be the bounded version. I could not write a self-test that distinguishes a true relation from a false one on this deck's own data, because 265.5 legitimately IS a generation figure under c3 AND legitimately IS the Crusoe One Load in the recital, which is GATE_LESSONS 20's shape: a true figure attached to the wrong population. The honest half to record is the second one the proposal names: deleting the sentence left the SLOPE asserting the same thing in geometry, and no gate here reads geometry.

frontier_scan.focus: span-level and pinpoint-citation verification, chosen because it is the class this run paid for
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_locator_: Is this Citation on Point? (arXiv 2608.12571) corrupts legal citations at three difficulties and measures whether a model catches it. Replacing the whole cited case: 93 to 100 percent recall. Changing ONLY the pinpoint page within the same case: 37 to 61 percent. The paper's conclusion is that models recognise the right legal topic without verifying support for the cited proposition. LePhantomCite (arXiv 2606.21155) reports the same asymmetry: AI reliably detects non-existent cases and name mismatches and struggles with pincites. A pinpoint locator is the single hardest thing for a reading model to check and one of the easiest things for a set-membership test to check, which is the argument for taking it off the judges and giving it to a gate.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_names_proposal_11: Not Wrong, But Untrue: LLM Overconfidence in Document-Based Queries (arXiv 2509.25498) names the failure as interpretive overreach: rather than inventing facts, models make analytical claims the documents did not support. That is exactly `260 load + 265.5 generation`, where every ingredient was sourced and the relation was not. It also shows why the obvious method would not have caught it: CLATTER (arXiv 2506.05243) decomposes a sentence into sub-facts and entails each one, and BOTH sub-facts here entail. A decomposition-and-aggregate checker PASSES this sentence. The relation needs a claim of its own, not a finer decomposition.
frontier_scan.the_generalisable_idea_worth_keeping: Hardware assertion-based verification has a name for the palette regex defect. An assertion A |-> B passes VACUOUSLY when A never becomes true, and the standard remedy is a COVER PROPERTY on the antecedent, asserted separately, so a suite can tell 'never violated' from 'never exercised'. Every gate in this repo that selects what to examine should carry one. GATE_LESSONS 26 already has half of it, where text_contrast prints the count it declined on success as well as on failure. Both gates touched this run now carry one: plan_render_check asserts every shipped storyboard yields at least five palette tokens, and locator_trace asserts the newest deck yields more than zero locator tokens.
frontier_scan.an_external_threshold_for_proposal_9_so_: The CIE gives the number this project would otherwise have had to measure off its own corpus, which the threshold rule in GATE_LESSONS warns is a ratchet. CIEDE2000 dE00 near 1.0 is a just noticeable difference, 2 to 3 is perceptible on close observation, above 5 is clearly visible. Computed here for the three collisions round 3's craft judge named against deck no. 8: satin_spar #F5F1E6 against cut_face #F4F0E4 is dE00 0.49, caliche_cap #E4DCC6 against limestone #E5DECC is 1.52, and ledge_shadow #241E22 against blackland #211E1A is 6.49. So two of the judge's three are at or under the JND and the third is a genuinely different colour, which is the case for measuring rather than eyeballing, in both directions. satin_spar at 0.49 is the deck's declared light and its type colour across nine frames, so the most-seen colour in deck no. 10 is deck no. 8's light under a new name, and no eye could have told you which of the three mattered.

2026-08-29.read_first: knowledge/shared/GATE_LESSONS.md, all 69 entries. out/2026-08-29/panel_rounds.jsonl, five rounds. The six candidates the launching phase ranked.
2026-08-29.the_run_this_came_out_of: Five panel rounds. Three of the holds were on defects the run had created in the round before, which is the case the routine's own rule about a number over the bar not being done exists for. All three upgrades below come from a hold this run actually took, and each one closes a gap where a green suite was measuring something narrower than it appeared to certify.

upgrades.what: scripts/carousel/numeral_trace.py. A numeral a frame prints must be reachable from a claim that frame cites, through that claim's quote, text, document title or url, or be a figure declared in aggregates.json.
upgrades.why: Round 4's hard fail. Six frames printed the eyebrow NSF AWARD 2535195 over a cite line naming c34, whose quote is the agency's news release about three new centres and contains no such number. Round 3 had introduced it: the run repaired an unsupported attribution by pointing the award number at a claim it had just fetched, and nobody checked whether that claim carried the number. The repair that held was to fetch the award record's own id field as c35 and cite that. This gate is what would have said so in round 1.
upgrades.why_every_other_gate_was_green: copy_sync_check proved the id RESOLVES, which it did, and its quotation half only reads text between quotation marks. Its own docstring says so under NOT COVERED, and an eyebrow is not a quotation. claims_check proved c34 is fetched and quoted. aggregate_check reads four aggregate SHAPES, a count, a duration, a span and a ratio, and an award number is none of them. label_guard skips numerals by an explicit [0-9-]+ test and skips any element carrying more than one claim id, which the cite line is. Five gates, five correct answers to four different questions, and none of them was the question.
upgrades.the_authorised_set_and_the_judgement_mad: quote, text, document and url of the claims THAT FRAME cites. Restricting to the quote alone was measured and rejected: it adds seven findings across the shipped decks and every one is correct work, because c5 of 2026-08-18 quotes one line of a daily schedule while its text carries the 110 and 90 minute blocks the run read off the same page. A gate that refuses the honest route teaches a run that the honest route fails. Document and url are in because that is where a docket or award number lives, and it is GATE_LESSONS 47's shape exactly: the exemption is earned per claim from that claim's own evidence, never granted by a list of numbers somebody typed.
upgrades.the_tokeniser_is_not_a_second_copy_of_ag: aggregate_check matches SHAPES and caps at four digits, so on 2535195 it would match 2535 and name a number nobody printed, which is GATE_LESSONS 16 and is why it must not be reused here. This splits on whitespace, strips the punctuation a writer puts around a token, and keeps what is entirely digits, commas and points. There is no shape to get wrong because no shape is being looked for. Entry 34 warns against two tokenisers for one alphabet and this is not that: one detects aggregate phrases, the other splits a string into words.
upgrades.measured_before_it_was_written: 86 frames over the ten decks shipped before this one, 205 numeral tokens, 15 untraced. Every one of the fifteen was read by hand and every one is real. 2026-08-22 prints PROJECT 58482 on three frames while fourteen claims carry that number and none of those three frames declares one of them. 2026-08-28 frame 2 prints 265.5 MW citing five claims with the figure in a sixth. 2026-08-28 frame 6 prints 100 MW, which no claim in that run carries at all. The 2026-08-29 deck as it shipped comes back clean.
upgrades.verification: python3 scripts/carousel/numeral_trace.py --self-test, by exit code, 38 assertions. The defect is replayed against the run's OWN COMMITTED claims.json, not a fixture: the round 4 frame citing c34 goes red and names c35 as the claim that has the number, and the round 5 frame citing c35 is clean. Same words, same frame, one id changed, which is the discrimination test GATE_LESSONS 36 asks for. The fifteen historic findings are pinned per deck as expected counts, so a later change to the matching rule that quietly dissolves them turns the self-test red. python3 scripts/carousel/shipped_check.py --run 2026-08-28 reports the two real findings as notes on an older deck, and gate_status --date 2026-08-29 prints the row PASS.
upgrades.wiring_because_a_self_test_is_not_wiring: Two places, both in this lane, because .github/workflows belongs to the human actor. gate_status.py computes the row INLINE rather than reading a receipt file, so it cannot be ABSENT once copy.json, claims.json and a render exist, and `numerals` is in STRICT_REQUIRED so the ship gate refuses a run that never produced it. shipped_check.py registers it CURRENT, which is what puts it in CI on every push, fatal on the newest deck and a note on older ones. That scope judgement is the one aggregates and locators already made and its reason is written at the call site: a gate written on 2026-08-29 turning eight shipped decks red is how a suite teaches a run to scroll past it.
upgrades.revert: delete scripts/carousel/numeral_trace.py, the `numerals` row in gate_status.rows_for, the entry in STRICT_REQUIRED, and g_numerals plus its GATES line in shipped_check.py
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a run starts writing claims whose quote or text is padded with a number so a frame can print it. That is the failure this gate makes tempting and it is worse than the defect, because a fabricated claim is permanent while a wrong citation is one line. The tell is a claim whose quote carries a figure that appears nowhere near it in the fetched document, and the message in the gate says FIX THE CITATION rather than write a claim for that reason. The other tell is the finding count rising above one or two a deck, which would mean the four-field authorised set is too narrow for how this product actually cites.

upgrades.what: .claude/skills/carousel-engine/qa.py now compares the deck's STANDING FURNITURE across frames and fails when a piece of it lays out on more lines on some frames than on others.
upgrades.why: All three judges opened round 4 with the same thing. Adding one claim id to the cover's foot pushed that flex row past its 920px measure, the line broke, and three frames printed the canonical URL as `texasaidocket.com01 /` with the counter alone on a second line. coherence_check.check_site_line reads the span's TEXT, finds texasaidocket.com, and passes. The DOM was right and the pixels were wrong, which is GATE_LESSONS' one sentence: a checker sees what it reads and the product is what a reader receives. CLAUDE.md's public URL section is specifically about that string, and the gate written for it is blind to the one way it can be rendered wrong.
upgrades.why_it_moved_out_of_the_frame: The run's own repair was a per-frame assertion measuring the foot's client rects, pasted into all nine slides. That is the right measurement in the wrong place. It protects one deck and every future deck has to remember to paste it, which is the shape of every defect this repo has shipped twice.
upgrades.no_threshold_was_typed_and_that_is_the_d: The assertion is a COMPARISON, not an absolute. Standing furniture is the text that appears on every frame, which is what coherence_check already calls the frame that does not vary, and the rule is that a piece of it takes the same number of lines on every frame. Six frames gave the counter one line and three gave it two: that is the finding, and it needs no opinion about how many lines a counter ought to have. GATE_LESSONS 10 is the entry for this, where two renderings are meant to agree, compare them rather than holding each to a number somebody typed.
upgrades.the_blind_spot_is_stated_and_asserted: If a row breaks on EVERY frame the counts agree and this says nothing. Closing that needs a number for how many lines furniture may have, which the compute-not-generate law forbids, so the honest cure is the frame-level assertion measuring a row against its own container, and that belongs in the frame contract. The self-test asserts the blind spot deliberately, by making the counter two lines on every frame and requiring silence, so nobody later mistakes it for a bug and bolts on a threshold.

frontier_scan.focus: layout faults invisible to DOM assertions, and identifier-level citation verification. Both were chosen because they are the two classes this run paid for, in rounds 4 and 5.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_numeral_: CiteAudit (arXiv 2602.23452) names the exact failure mode as its own category, Identifier Fabrication, and describes it in a sentence that could have been written about round 4: an identifier resolves to a real work, but the visible citation text describes a different one. Its own note is that these are hard to detect through surface-level similarity because the citation appears structurally complete while being invalid, which is why copy_sync_check passed. Its dataset is 6,475 real and 2,967 fake citations and the fakes include DOI and identifier hallucinations specifically because they cannot be caught by text similarity alone. HALLMARK (arXiv 2607.18360) diagnoses three failure modes in citation verifiers and is the paper to read before widening the authorised set here.
frontier_scan.how_that_changed_the_design: It is the argument for checking the NUMBER against the cited claim rather than checking that the claim exists. This repo already had the second, in copy_sync_check, and had it since 2026-08-12. The gap between them is exactly the gap the benchmark measures.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_the_furn: ReDeCheck and the responsive layout literature behind it (Walsh, Software Testing Verification and Reliability, 2020, and the SIGSOFT ISSTA 2017 tool paper) detect layout failures WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT ORACLE by building a Responsive Layout Graph and comparing alignment constraints across renderings, rather than by asserting absolute geometry. The failures it names are elements protruding, overlapping, or INCORRECTLY WRAPPING TO THE NEXT LINE, which is this run's foot row named in the literature's own words. The design consequence is the one taken above: the comparison is the oracle, so no threshold has to be typed.
frontier_scan.the_thing_worth_knowing_that_was_not_use: The 2026 industry writing on visual regression is unanimous that DOM assertions are structurally incapable of seeing truncated text and layout shift, and unanimous that the answer is a vision model comparing screenshots. That is a real technique and it is the wrong one here. A screenshot diff has no opinion about which difference matters, and this product's whole design is that the art varies every run, so a pixel comparison between decks would be noise from the first frame. Comparing a deck against ITSELF, frame to frame, over the parts that are supposed to be identical, is the same idea with a subject narrow enough to be an oracle.

frontier_scan.focus: constraint induced collapse of output variety, and conflict between two instructions given to one writer. Chosen because that is the class this run paid for, seven times.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_most_justifies_the_capt: ConInstruct (arXiv 2511.14342) benchmarks whether models detect conflicting constraints and what they do about them. Detection is strong, 87.3 F1 for Claude 4.5 Sonnet and 91.5 for DeepSeek R1, and the paper's headline is that models 'rarely explicitly notify users about the conflicts or request clarification when faced with conflicting constraints'. They resolve them silently. That is this defect exactly. The caption room met the refusal, resolved it by switching to the close that passes, and said nothing, seven runs running, and the fix that follows is not better detection. It is making the resolution stated where the next writer reads it, which is what the message and the doctrine section now do.
frontier_scan.the_second_finding: Evaluating the Diversity and Quality of LLM Generated Content (arXiv 2504.12522) argues for EFFECTIVE semantic diversity, meaning diversity measured only among outputs that clear a quality threshold, because diversity without quality is trivial. Read the other way round it is the warning this run needed. A variety ledger that records what was used without recording what was AVAILABLE under the constraints in force will report a healthy menu while one option is the only legal one. That is the argument for the doctrine marking the fifth substance unavailable rather than leaving five names on a list.
frontier_scan.the_third: Work on n-gram novelty finds that more constrained decoding strategies decrease novelty, which is the mechanism here in one sentence and is worth remembering the next time a hard form rule is added to any surface. Ask what it costs the variety ledger on the day it is written.
frontier_scan.not_pursued: Verbalized Sampling and the geometric mode collapse regulators are about sampling inside a model and there is nothing in this pipeline to apply them to. The caption is written by an agent under a brief, and the lever here is the brief and the ledger.

2026-09-04.the_run_this_came_out_of: Carousel 15 shipped a nine frame deck about a facial biometric test on the pedestrian exit lane at the Progreso International Bridge. Three judges, working independently, found FIVE on-frame strings dressed as the source's own words that no claim carries, and every gate in the suite was green on all five. upgrades.what: New gate `scripts/carousel/verbatim_check.py`. A dossier that seats a fragment of a source's own words on a frame lists it under a `verbatim:` key, filed under the claim whose QUOTE carries it, and every listed string must be a literal substring of that quote after a stated normalisation and must actually be on the frame. Beside it, a second direction that needs no declaration: where a frame prints one all-caps label that IS a literal fragment of a quote, every other label in the same RENDERED STYLE on that frame is listed for a human if it traces to no claim.
upgrades.why: Measured on this run's own artifacts. `IT DID JUST THAT` was in no claim quote at all. `HIGH QUALITY IMAGES` dropped `facial` out of c9's `high-quality facial images`, in a verbatim slot, beside a real quotation. `MARYLAND, ROOFED` and `PROGRESO, OPEN SKY` were physical assertions about two real places and the second contradicted the deck's own frame 1. `CARRIL DE CAPTURA` and `CARRIL DE EXCLUSION` were Spanish sign text on a frame whose subject is what the signs said, where c13 says only that the signs were in English and Spanish. `label_guard` reads the capitalised run beside a claim id, so a plate in the art region with the citation chip a third of a frame away was never in its window. `noun_trace` warns on named THINGS, and a sentence names no thing.
upgrades.why_a_declaration_and_not_a_detector: Measured rather than argued. An auto-discovering draft that treated any style slot holding a quoted anchor as a verbatim slot was replayed across all fifteen shipped decks and went RED ON THE REPAIRED DECK OF 2026-09-04, on frame 3, where `AND AIFI` is a line-wrapped tail of `PARAVISION AND AIFI` and `SOLUTION 1` beside it is a legitimate authored label. knowledge/carousel/TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY.md records what happens to a gate that fires on correct behaviour. So the hard half takes a declaration, and the discovery half survives as a list that decides nothing, with an anchor forbidden from opening on a conjunction.
upgrades.what_the_two_halves_actually_catch: Replayed against this run's real render report rather than against a fixture. Restore the deck the panel saw, which is c31 removed from claims.json and `FACIAL` taken back out of frame 8's second plate, and the DISCOVERY half names both fabrications with no declaration anywhere in the storyboard and is silent on the repaired deck. Frame 4's two place assertions and frame 6's two sign strings are caught only where the dossier declares them, because their slots hold no quoted anchor to discover. That limit is stated in the gate's own docstring rather than papered over, and the answer to it is the spec.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/verbatim_check.py --self-test` exits 0 and replays all five strings, each failing when declared and each repaired form passing, plus a misattribution case, a declared-but-never-drawn case, an unknown claim id, a claim with no quote, and the empty-versus-absent distinction. It also runs the DECLARED half against all fifteen shipped decks and asserts none of them fails, and asserts the newest shipped deck draws no discovery note. RED ON THE REAL ARTIFACT: rebuild out/2026-09-04/ into a scratch directory with c31 dropped, `HIGH-QUALITY FACIAL IMAGES` replaced by `HIGH QUALITY IMAGES` and a `verbatim:` block added to slide 8's dossier, and the gate exits 1 naming both. Put the repair back and it exits 0 with `3 declared fragment(s), every one a literal substring of its own claim's quote`. `gate_status.py --self-test` exits 0 with four new cases on the row, including that a receipt declaring nothing is WARN and never PASS.
upgrades.the_self_test_caught_its_own_author: The first draft of the frame 4 repaired case filed `MARYLAND TEST FACILITY` under c30, and the gate refused it, correctly: c30's quote says `a replica of the pedestrian exit environment at MdTF` and never spells the facility out. Those are c3's words. The case stays in the file as written, with the misattribution branch asserted beside it, because GATE_LESSONS 16 says a fixture written beside a detector agrees with it and this one did not.
upgrades.revert: the commit named below. Reverting removes the gate, the gate_status row and the spec section together.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a run writes a correct `verbatim:` block and the gate refuses a string the source plainly does say, the normalisation is too strict and the failure will name a punctuation difference rather than a word. It is loose in one direction by construction, so that would be a bug rather than a threshold. If the discovery half starts naming more than about one slot per deck, its anchor rule has drifted and it should be measured across the shipped corpus again before anybody widens it. And if six months of dossiers carry no `verbatim:` key at all, the declaration was too expensive to write and the answer is the spec or the prompt, never a detector that guesses.

upgrades.what: `scripts/carousel/panel_ready.py` measures the deck's value arc against the plan the storyboard declares, and refuses to call the deck scorable when the deck median L* misses its own planned median by more than one Munsell value step.
upgrades.why: out/2026-09-04/measurements.json records it. The first render of carousel 15 measured deck median 6.3 against a plan of 24, with eight of nine frames between 4.5 and 10.1, which is not a dark deck but an unlit one. It was found by the showrunner writing a one-off measure.py AFTER three judges had been spawned on it, which is precisely what panel_ready exists to prevent. Every prior deck missed its own plan too: 2026-08-29 planned near 32 and measured 15.6, 2026-08-30 planned 40 and measured 21.2, 2026-09-02 planned 30 and measured 20.4. The artwork ledger recorded every one of those honestly. A ledger that records an outcome is not a gate that refuses one.
upgrades.the_tolerance_and_why_that_number: One Munsell value step, 10.0 L*. Munsell value is the perceptually uniform lightness scale and adjacent values are one plainly visible step apart by construction: under ASTM D1535 the luminance factors for V=4 and V=5 give L* 41.2 and 51.8, and the step holds near 10 at the dark end too, V=1 being L* 10.4 and V=2 being 20.5. It is deliberately NOT derived from our own decks, because GATE_LESSONS' rule for setting a threshold says a figure measured off our own corpus and re-derived is a ratchet with no floor, and four planned-against-measured pairs is not a distribution. What those four say, recorded in the file for whoever revisits it: three of the four clear one step and the fourth sits just inside it, so this fires on the size of miss the evidence shows and stays quiet on the repaired deck, which measured 23.1 against 24.
upgrades.the_parse_rule_is_stated_and_was_taken_o: Two shapes. A fenced block whose lines read `F1  24  the lane`, under a paragraph naming the value arc, which is what 2026-09-04 writes and what the spec asks for. And an inline comma list after the word `planned` inside a value-arc paragraph, which is what 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-30 write. Both are scoped to the cue's own paragraph, so a comma list elsewhere in a plan cannot become an arc, and 2026-09-03's storyboard, which records a MEASUREMENT and no plan, is read as declaring nothing. A plan and a render of different lengths REFUSES to compare rather than guessing which side is stale. A deck declaring no arc is silent and says so on its own line, because nine of fifteen shipped storyboards declare none.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/panel_ready.py --self-test` exits 0. It replays this run's two real arrays: the first render at 6.3 against a plan of 24 is CAUGHT and the repaired deck at 23.1 against the same plan passes. A miss of 9.6, which is 2026-09-02's real miss and sits inside one Munsell step, is not a finding, and a miss of 10.1 is. The parse rule is asserted against all three real shipped shapes and against every shipped storyboard that declares an arc, requiring one value per frame, so a run writing it a fourth way goes red rather than silent. RED ON THE REAL ARTIFACT: copy out/2026-09-04/render/*.png into a scratch directory with every frame but the light one scaled to 22 percent, keep the real storyboard, and check_value_arc reports deck median 3.2 against a plan of 24 and returns a finding. On the shipped PNGs, `panel_ready.py --date 2026-09-04` exits 0 and prints `deck median 23 against a plan of 24`.
upgrades.what_it_does_not_decide: The plan is the run's own document and lives in the `daily` lane, so a run can rewrite the arc rather than redraw the frames. This gate is a forcing function to make the run LOOK before it spends three judges, not a lock, and the failure message says to do one or the other and record which. Making it a lock would need the arc in a lane the run cannot reach, which is a different change and probably a worse one.
upgrades.revert: the commit named below.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a deck goes red here while the frames are plainly right at thumbnail size, the plan was written as an aspiration rather than as a measurement and the fix is upstream in how the arc is chosen. If it never fires again across ten decks, either the machine got better, which the printed line will show, or the parse went quiet, which the per-storyboard assertion in the self-test is there to catch.

upgrades.what: `scripts/carousel/dedupe_check.py` prints every `angle_note` inside the ledger's own window, first, before its own verdict, whether or not anything else fires. It never changes the exit code.
upgrades.why: ledger/carousel/topics.json, deck 14's angle_note: `FOURTH DECK IN SEVEN BUILT ON WHAT A DOCUMENT DOES NOT SAY... THE NEXT RUN SHOULD PICK A STORY WHERE SOMETHING HAPPENED, not one where a document is quiet.` Deck 11's said the same thing about opening moves. Carousel 15's angle is that a document is quiet, the fifth in eight, and both round 1 judges named it. Three consecutive notes, 2026-08-26, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-03, each say IN THE NOTE ITSELF that dedupe_check cannot see this field, which is as clear a statement of a machine defect as this project has ever written down. The field was written for the selection phase and read by nothing at the moment it mattered.
upgrades.why_it_warns_and_will_never_fail: An angle is a judgement, and a gate that refused one would be a gate deciding editorial. This file's own docstring already says the tool removes the luck and the showrunner keeps the call. A note the run has read and disagreed with is a decision. A note nobody read is the failure, and reading is the whole of what was missing.
upgrades.the_window_is_read_not_typed: Every note inside the ledger's own `window_days`, which is the same window the repeat test uses. A count typed here would be a second opinion about how far back a lesson reaches. Three of fourteen entries carry a note today, so it is three paragraphs rather than a wall.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/dedupe_check.py --self-test` exits 0 with six new cases: deck 14's instruction is surfaced whole rather than truncated to a title, a note outside the window is not carried forward, a blank note is not a note, a ledger with none surfaces nothing rather than raising, and surfacing changes no score and no band. It also asserts against the SHIPPED topics.json that the field parses and that at least one note is live on the newest entry's own date, so the day a run spells the field differently this goes red rather than going quiet, which is the exact failure the upgrade exists to close. Run against the real ledger with this deck's own entities it prints all three notes above the verdict and exits 0.
upgrades.revert: the commit named below.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a run reads three notes and still builds the fifth quiet-document deck in nine, printing was not the lever and the next move is the one filed in the backlog: the selection phase quotes the notes it read into the run record, so ignoring one has to be said out loud. If the notes ever run past about half a screen, the window is carrying more than a run will read and the ledger, not this gate, is where that gets decided.

frontier_scan.focus: holding generated text to its own source span. Rotated deliberately away from 2026-08-21's entailment question, which reached the right answer with the wrong dependency.
frontier_scan.the_finding_that_shaped_the_gate: Quotation verification separates two errors that a similarity score cannot: a quotation absent from the source altogether, and one present with a word removed that changes its scope. `IT DID JUST THAT` is the first kind. `HIGH QUALITY IMAGES` is the second and is the harder one, because every word in it is in the source and in that order. A literal substring test over a normalised span catches both. A bag of words or a token overlap ratio catches only the first, and would have scored the second above almost any threshold. That is why the check landed as a substring rather than as a ratio, and why the normalisation is loose on punctuation and strict on words.
frontier_scan.refused_again_for_the_reason_2026-08-21_: An entailment model as a gate. CI installs pyyaml and nothing else, GATE_LESSONS 15 is the entry about a gate that passed fifteen times locally and failed on the first push for exactly that, and a verdict that moves when a model moves is not a verdict a project whose whole argument is recomputability gets to publish.
frontier_scan.the_second_finding_worth_keeping: Perceptual lightness scales are the right family of external standard for a value target, because they are defined by equal visible steps rather than by equal signal. That is what let the arc tolerance be an outside number instead of a fraction of our own spread, and GATE_LESSONS' own rule for setting a threshold is that an external standard cannot creep because it was never derived from us.

2026-09-05.phase: retro and upgrade, deck no. 16, actor `upgrade`
2026-09-05.revert_commit: the commit this phase makes. One commit carries all three upgrades and each is independent inside it, one file each: scripts/carousel/texan_check.py, scripts/carousel/label_guard.py and scripts/carousel/aggregate_check.py. Reverting the whole commit removes all three and reverting one file removes one, with no shared code between them.
2026-09-05.what_this_phase_chose_and_why: Ten findings came out of this run and every one of them was found by a judge, a pixel critic or the showrunner reading. The three that landed are the three where a MEASUREMENT could have made the same finding for nothing, and all three are the same disease: a gate whose answer about the product was wrong while its exit code was right. Two report a false thing and one reports nothing at all. The ranking was by judge time, not by interest, and the seven that did not land are written out with their measurements in knowledge/carousel/UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md so the next phase does not re-derive them.

upgrades.what: `texan_check.gazetteer()` reads the principal cities out of each statistical area's own delineated name, so the four largest cities in Texas are places this gate can see.
upgrades.why: Carousel no. 16 is a story about a University of Houston led team and prints `The Houston led team` on frame 4, and this gate reported `places NONE`. `assets/geo/tx-places.json` carries 254 counties, 67 CBSAs, 13 CSAs, 2 divisions and NO CITIES, so the only string in the file carrying Houston as a city is the metro's full name `Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands`, which no deck has ever written. The one bare Houston in the file is Houston COUNTY in East Texas. Measured across sixteen shipped decks with a copy.json on 2026-09-05, this gate reported no place on SIX decks that name Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth or Houston in plain prose. That is the gate whose entire subject is whether a Texan can tell where this happened, blind to the four biggest cities in the state, on 0.30 of the rubric that the backlog says nobody ever attacks.
upgrades.why_the_fix_is_the_file_and_not_a_typed_: OMB names a statistical area after its principal cities joined with hyphens, so the delineated name is already a machine readable statement that Houston, Pasadena and The Woodlands are cities. Splitting on the hyphen reads that statement rather than restating it, which matters because assets/ is not this lane's and a typed city list would be a second source of truth for a fact the gazetteer already carries.
upgrades.the_two_guards_on_the_split: A row that leaves Texas contributes nothing, because `El Paso-Las Cruces, TX-NM` would otherwise teach this gate that a New Mexico city is a Texas place. Only rows whose full_name ends `, TX` contribute, which costs Texarkana and buys a miss instead of a misreport. And a city name standing at the head of another place's name is that other place, so `Houston County` and `Houston ISD` are not the city. Without that second guard the 2026-08-18 calibration gains a Houston off `Houston ISD`.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/texan_check.py --self-test` exits 0 with five new assertions and two new calibration rows. RED WITHOUT THE FIX, measured rather than asserted: a copy of the file with the split and the tail guard removed exits 1 with four failures, naming `a deck naming the city of Houston reports it` returning [] and the 2026-09-05 row measuring none. REPLAYED ACROSS SEVENTEEN SHIPPED DECKS: the split adds seven place findings, Houston on 2026-08-18's own city, Dallas and Houston on 2026-08-21, Fort Worth on 2026-08-25, Austin on 2026-08-26, 2026-08-27, 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-02, and each was read in context before this line was written. It removes exactly one, a duplicate `Lubbock` on 2026-08-25 whose copy's only Lubbock is `Lubbock County`. `texan_check --date 2026-09-05` now prints `places Houston` where it printed NONE.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a deck ever reports a place it does not name, the length floor is carrying more than it can and the answer is a shape rule like the county one rather than a longer word. Alice, Paris, Palestine, Temple and Mission are all principal cities and all ordinary words, and none of them fired on seventeen decks, which is evidence and not a guarantee. If the gazetteer ever gains real city rows, this split becomes redundant and should be deleted rather than left to agree with the new rows by luck.

upgrades.what: `label_guard` masks the deck's own wordmark, read from `config/brand.yaml`, as a PHRASE.
upgrades.why: The FURNITURE set says in its own comment that it holds `the deck's own furniture` and it holds none: connectives and the generic half of a body's name, and nothing else. Every frame ends in a colophon, and where that colophon is one element the mark stands directly before the claim ids, `TEXAS AI DOCKETc17 c18`. So the six word window walks back off the id and picks up the masthead. Replayed across seventeen shipped decks this is 2026-08-30 slide 9, where the gate reports TEXAS, AI and DOCKET as three unsupported labels beside c40, and it is what fired on carousel no. 16's colophon and its RICE NEWS byline. Three findings on one frame, none of them a claim about what a body did, on a gate whose whole value is that a run reads its findings.
upgrades.why_a_phrase_and_never_words: This is `_place_mask`'s argument one function over. A set of single words would make a lone AI furniture on every frame in the deck, and AI beside a claim id is the assertion this gate should be reading hardest. A one word mark is deliberately NOT exempted: if the mark ever becomes one word this gate starts firing on it, loudly, which is the direction a selector is allowed to fail in.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/label_guard.py --self-test` exits 0 with three new cases: the mark beside a claim id is not a label, a lone word of the mark beside a claim that never says it IS still a label, and the mark comes back non empty from brand.yaml or the case fails rather than testing nothing. RED WITHOUT THE FIX: a copy of the file with the one masking line removed exits 1 and names TEXAS, AI and DOCKET beside c41. REPLAYED ACROSS SEVENTEEN SHIPPED DECKS: 2026-08-30 goes from 35 findings to 32, which is exactly the three masthead words, and every other deck's finding count is byte for byte unchanged.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a deck ever prints a real claim label that happens to be the three words of the mark in that order, this would pass it, which is a shape no frame has ever drawn and would be visible in the render anyway. The likelier failure is brand.yaml moving the key, which would make the mask silently empty, so the self-test asserts the mark parses non empty rather than trusting it.

upgrades.what: `aggregate_check` stops reading a count of one as a tally.
upgrades.why: Carousel no. 16's caption asked `Which one does ARPA-E publish?` and this gate reported `one does` as a computed count, so the run reworded a correct sentence around a figure that was never there. The count shape requires a PLURAL noun and `does` is a verb ending in s, which is the whole of the mis-parse: `one` before any word ending in s reads as a tally of that word. English can't quantify a plural noun with one, so a count whose numeral resolves to 1 is never a tally. Replayed over every published surface of seventeen shipped decks, this shape fires ten times with a numeral of one and NOT ONE of the ten is an aggregate: `one falls`, `one that publishes`, `One says`, `One reads`, `one news`, `one line per fact this`, `one does`, `one project the release does`, `01 ADS Incident Reports`, `One and Crusoe Two loads`. A gate that misreports a figure is worse than one that misses it, and this is that defect ten times over on work that shipped clean.
upgrades.what_it_does_not_eat: A scale word after the numeral means the figure is not one. WORDS stops at twenty, so `one hundred filings` matches with `one` as its numeral and the real figure is 100. That phrase stays detected and stays declarable. Nothing else is lost, because a tally of one is written `one filing` and the count shape has never been able to see a singular noun.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/aggregate_check.py --self-test` exits 0 with seven new assertions, five of them the real strings measured off shipped decks rather than invented. 2026-09-05.a_mistake_this_phase_made_and_did_not_hi: THIS PHASE DESTROYED AN UNCOMMITTED DAILY LANE EDIT TO ledger/docket.json AND IT HAS NOT BEEN RESTORED. Mid phase, `git status` showed that file reindented from two spaces to one with equal line counts in and out, and the visible hunk was pure whitespace. Reading that as a stray reformat by something this phase had run, it was reverted with `git checkout -- ledger/docket.json`. It was neither stray nor whitespace. Equal line counts are also what a same length string edit produces, and the daily lane was concurrently striking a refuted reading from item tx-2026-0124. The proof arrived one step later: `docs/` still held the NEW wording and `site_fresh_check` went red against the reverted ledger, and the run then rebuilt `docs/` from the old ledger, so the tree is now internally consistent and the record repair is missing. THE TWO STRINGS, RECOVERED FROM docs/item/tx-2026-0124/index.md BEFORE THE REBUILD. Title: `Energy Department research arm funds a Houston led team using AI to search for new magnet materials`. The summary's last sentence: `The stated goal is to find entirely new materials while balancing supply constraint concerns.` The committed ledger still says `...using AI to design magnets that avoid imported rare earths` and `The stated target is a magnet that outperforms neodymium iron boron while cutting dependence on foreign mineral supply`, which is the refuted reading commit 6bd8f89c says it struck. Any OTHER field of that item that changed in the same edit is not recoverable, because only the title and the summary render into index.md. ledger/docket.json is the public record and is NOT this lane's, so this phase did not write it back, which is the same boundary that made the loss possible. THE LESSON, and it is the one this repository already states twice about explanations: a diff whose insertions equal its deletions is not evidence of a whitespace change, and `git checkout --` on a shared working tree destroys work no reflog can return. A phase that shares a tree with a live run reverts nothing it did not write.

what_was_considered_and_not_built.extracting universals mechanically in qu: The 2026-09-04 backlog filed this for the next upgrade phase and this is that phase, so the measurement it asked for was made and it says WAIT. UNIVERSAL is a double allowlist, seven quantifier words against twenty set nouns, and this run's two misses are both outside it: slide 9's `No material named yet.` and the caption's `Three years is the only schedule in the record.` Neither `no` nor `only` is in the pattern, which is GATE_LESSONS 39 exactly. Measured across every published surface of sixteen decks with surfaces, the current pattern raises 18 findings and the widened word set raises 240, thirteen times the noise, about fifteen a deck. A gate raising fifteen undeclarable warnings a deck is a row that is always red, which GATE_LESSONS 16 says is ignored exactly as fast as one that is always green. So the honest state is that the defect is real, the naive fix is worse than the defect, and the narrowing has not been found. The 240 hits are reproducible in one pass and the backlog now carries the counts so the next phase starts from the measurement rather than from the hunch.
what_was_considered_and_not_built.plan_render_check's REQUIRED_STR firing: Refused as a gate change, filed as doctrine. The item `the note reads 'X'. It read 'Y', which no claim carries` fails because the gate demands the frame print 'Y' too, and it cost two edit rounds. Every discriminator tried was a tense test, and English `read` is ambiguous between a past singular and a present plural, so `the two plates read 'A' and 'B'` would have been silently exempted. That is a false negative bought with a false positive, on a gate whose subject is whether the plan describes the frame. The vocabulary to say this already exists and is already checked: FORBIDDEN_BEFORE handles `the note reads 'X' and never reads 'Y'`. So the resolution is an authoring rule in SLIDE_DOSSIER_SPEC.md, which is this lane, not an exemption in the gate. FILED AND NOT WRITTEN, because three upgrades had already landed with a replay each and a fourth change would ship without one, and because a doctrine paragraph with no gate behind it is exactly the prose this project keeps proving is not a boundary. The wording is in knowledge/carousel/UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md, ready to lift, and the pairing it needs is plan_render_check's failure message naming FORBIDDEN_BEFORE so the next writer reads the resolution instead of inferring it.

upgrades.what: `plan_render_check` compares the claim set every frame declares against every artifact that declares it: the dossier's `claims:` list, the dossier's `numerals:` sources, `copy.json`'s per-slide list, and the claim strip the frame actually prints.

upgrades.measured_over_seventeen_shipped_decks_be: strip against plan, drift on 5 decks and 9 frames. copy.json against plan, drift on 8 decks and 12 frames. Six of those copy side frames print no strip at all, which is why the copy surface is read and not only the rendered one: printing a strip is a design choice a frame may decline, and copy.json exists for every deck this project has built. The deck that shipped today is clean on all of it, 18 comparisons over 9 frames, because the run repaired five of these by hand.
upgrades.the_relation_is_equality_and_that_is_a_j: The spec defines the list as every factual string on the slide, so a strip printing fewer ids than the plan declares is a frame under citing a fact a reader cannot trace, and one printing more is a plan that no longer describes the frame. Both directions are named in the message.
upgrades.two_things_it_had_to_get_right: A strip split across separate text nodes is ONE strip, because 2026-08-19's slide 8 renders c3, c19, c20 and c21 as four nodes and reading the first alone reports a correct frame as citing one claim. And a node reading `CLAIM c7. QUOTED VERBATIM.`, which is 2026-08-16's slide 3, is a sentence about a claim rather than a citation strip, so the pattern is anchored to the whole node.
upgrades.verification: `plan_render_check.py --self-test` exits 0 with sixteen new assertions, two of them against the SHIPPED artifacts rather than fixtures: 2026-09-05's slide 1 declares `c18 c17` and both its frame and its copy say `c18` alone, and 2026-09-07 comes back silent with every frame compared on both surfaces. RED WITHOUT THE FIX, forced twice and measured rather than asserted. Removing the claims block in place turns 12 assertions red including both shipped deck rows. Replacing the strip reader with the naive first matching node version turns exactly one red, the split node case, which is the assertion proving the input can tell a working implementation from a broken one. `plan_render_check --date 2026-09-07` exits 0 and `shipped_check` exits 0 over all seventeen decks, where the historical drift lands as a note because that gate is registered CURRENT scope.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a deck legitimately wants its strip to cite a SUBSET of the claims the plan lists, this is the wrong relation and the answer is to change the spec's definition of the field first and this gate second, never the other way round. The tell would be a run repeatedly widening a dossier's claims list to match a strip it meant to keep short. And if a frame ever prints claim ids in a form this pattern cannot read, the `uncited_slides` count rises silently for that frame, which is why the count is printed on success as well as on failure.

Two different machines at two different universities share no distinctive word. `topics.json`'s own `angle_note` field has complained about this blindness at decks 8, 11, 14 and 17, in prose, to nothing that could act on it.

That ledger is the `daily` lane's, the field would need writing by a phase this lane cannot edit, and every entry already committed would carry nothing, so a gate keyed on it would be asleep for a month and then depend on a run remembering. The record ALREADY carries the classification, computed and schema checked: every deck names its docket item and every docket item carries `topic`. Joining the two reads a fact that exists rather than asking for a new one.
upgrades.measured_on_the_shipped_ledgers: Three of the last four decks and four of the last seven sit on `research-and-science`, and nothing anywhere reported it. upgrades.it_never_changes_the_exit_code: Stated in the file and asserted in the self-test. A beat is not a repeat, four genuinely different decisions can share one, and a gate that refused a beat would be a gate deciding editorial, which this file's own docstring refuses. Making the record unreadable turns the real artifact assertion red, and it did NOT the first time I tried it, because that block was guarded by `if both ledgers are readable` and simply disappeared. upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a run starts choosing a story to satisfy the beat report rather than reading it, the tool has become a verdict and the fix is to make it quieter, not louder. upgrades.what: `texan_check` reads the run's OWN FETCHED EVIDENCE, the snapshots in `sources/` as well as `claims.json`, and when the deck names no Texas place it names the places the evidence carries and the file each came from.

upgrades.scoped_to_the_zero_case_on_purpose: Where a deck already names a place its evidence usually names more, and 2026-08-30's claims carry seventeen against a deck that correctly names one. Reporting that gap every run is nine findings a deck that are not defects, which is how a gate teaches a run to scroll past the tenth. The finding is a deck naming NONE while its own evidence names one. The count of evidence files scanned is printed either way, so a scan that had nothing to read cannot read as a scan that found nothing.
upgrades.verification: `texan_check.py --self-test` exits 0 with eight new assertions. The fixture sentence is VERBATIM out of the run's own horizon.txt rather than written to suit the detector, GATE_LESSONS 16, and two assertions read the real snapshots where the container still has them and SAY SO when it does not, because out/ is gitignored and absent in CI. upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: If a run starts putting a place on a frame because this named it, rather than because the story is about that place, the tool has become an instruction and it should be reworded. Round Rock is the successor's room and Frontera sits at UT Austin in Travis County, so the honest use of this reading is to check which machine a place belongs to before printing it. frontier_scan.focus: how a reference table goes stale with nothing reporting it, which is the area the 2026-09-05 phase handed forward as the one never rotated to
frontier_scan.finding: A static reference table does not go stale on a clock, so a freshness check is the wrong instrument, and the data quality literature gets this backwards in as many words. What goes stale is the AGREEMENT between the vintage a table declares and the answers a consumer derives from it, so the check belongs at the CONSUMER and it is a canary rather than a timestamp. Concrete instances found: Connecticut retired county FIPS 09001 through 09015 in 2022 for planning regions coded 09110 to 09190, so a table keyed on the old codes still parses, still joins and quietly returns nothing for a whole state, and OMB Bulletin 23-01 redelineated the CBSAs in July 2023 under standards that carry a process for mid decade updates.
frontier_scan.why_it_lands_here: `assets/geo/tx-places.json` declares its vintage honestly as the OMB July 2023 delineation and stamps every place with `provenance.metro: omb-2023-delineation`, and NOTHING in this repository reads either string. `texan_check.gazetteer()` derives its entire city set by splitting each statistical area's delineated name on its hyphens, which is the correct reading of what OMB publishes and means the day the gazetteer is rebuilt against a later delineation the set of cities that gate can see changes in silence. The practice worth copying is the one RNA-seq tooling uses, propagating a reference checksum into the output so an analysis can be told which reference it was computed against, and the consequence is the one Firefox shipped with stale bundled tzdata: wrong answers rather than errors.
frontier_scan.the_next_step_it_suggests: One file, in this lane, not built today only because three is the ceiling. `texan_check` reads the vintage the gazetteer declares and asserts it is the one its calibration was measured against, so a rebuild says recalibrate me instead of changing its answers. The canary is the handful of answers the gate is known to depend on and its self test already half carries them.
