upgrades.what: `plan_render_check.acceptance_items` reads the WHOLE acceptance list. PyYAML is the primary route, the same parser `dossier_check` has always used on the same blocks, and a continuation-aware regex is the fallback for a block PyYAML refuses.
upgrades.why: The block was taken with `^acceptance:\s*\n((?:  - .*\n)+)`, whose repetition ends at the first line that is not two spaces and a dash. That is the continuation of an item long enough to wrap, so THE BLOCK ENDED AT THE FIRST WRAPPED ITEM and everything after it in that slide's list was never read. The gate has been certifying a fraction of every plan since it was written, and it is the gate that exists because the plan-versus-render defect shipped in all three of this project's early runs.
upgrades.measured_on_the_real_artifact_before_a_l: The 2026-09-08 storyboard as it was first written, at commit 7a32b69e: 17 acceptance items read of 52. Per slide the parser saw 1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1 and 5 where 6, 5, 7, 5, 5, 6, 5, 6 and 7 were written. The items that survive truncation are the SHORT ones, and a short item is the one least likely to quote a string, which is why the gate then reported `0 of 16 acceptance items carry a machine-checkable assertion`. Three frames rendered outside their own declared median L* and no gate said so, because every one of those declarations sits past a wrapped item.
upgrades.verification: Four new self-test cases and they are two different kinds. SYNTHETIC: a four item acceptance list whose first item wraps. The gate reads four, joins the wrapped item rather than cutting it, and the parser this replaced is kept inline in the test and asserted to read ONE of the four, so the replay is visible rather than described. The forbidden-string item is deliberately the LAST of the four, the one truncation ate, and `check()` is asserted to still fail on a render that prints it, which proves the recovered items are enforced and not merely counted. REAL ARTIFACT: the yaml route and the text fallback are compared over all 158 dossiers in every storyboard under runs/carousel/, and disagreement on any one of them fails. That half is GATE_LESSONS entry 50 ("A security fix moved one line, and the pre-push runner went red on every clean checkout"), where the synthetic case proves the logic can tell two shapes apart and only the case that reads the shipped file would have gone red the day it broke. Ran clean on out/2026-09-08 as well, at 12 of 77.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: The checkable count on a shipped deck falls rather than rises, which would mean the yaml route is silently returning nothing and the fallback is not being reached. Or the count rises and the gate starts failing on frames that are correct, which would mean a wrapped item's joined text is being matched as a quoted needle it never was on one line. The self-test's shipped-dossier sweep is what carries the first; the second reads as a burst of `does not print it` failures on a deck nobody changed.

upgrades.what: `sources_block` prints its day count provenance line only when an aggregate carries `from_date` and `to_date` and the two differ, rather than when an aggregate is labelled `kind: duration` or `kind: span`.
upgrades.why: `kind` is a label a writer types, and every duration a source states in its own words is legitimately labelled `duration` too. So the sentence `Day counts computed in compute.py from the source dates above.` rode along on decks that performed no subtraction anywhere. That is a provenance claim, made to a reader, about a computation that did not happen, published by the one file whose own docstring says no count and no date in its output is typed there. GATE_LESSONS entry 41 ("A fact the code branches on, carried only in prose") is the rule this is a case of, one level up from a numeral: a fact the build BRANCHES ON needs a field, because a decision derived from a label is a decision derived from whatever wording somebody used that day.
upgrades.it_reached_readers_and_that_is_why_it_ra: runs/carousel/2026-08-30/first_comment.txt carries the line. That deck's only two durations are SIX MONTHS quoted from c21 and three years quoted from c17, each carrying `quoted_from` and each carrying a note reading in as many words `Quoted in the source's own wording. No arithmetic, no unit change, no hedge dropped.` It nearly shipped again on 2026-09-08, where both instances of `four weeks` are quoted verbatim from c17, and a scoring judge caught it in the round rather than a gate. The gate's own comment already recorded an integrity judge calling this exact line a hard fail on 2026-08-26, and the first repair fixed the unconditional case and left the label case open.
upgrades.verification: Eleven new self-test cases. The two shapes side by side, so the discrimination is stated rather than implied. `build()` itself is exercised in both directions, because a predicate that is right while its caller ignores it is GATE_LESSONS entry 37 ("A law with no mechanism, reported as a skip"). Then the real artifact half, four shipped aggregate files with the answer asserted per date: 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-08 withheld, 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-19 earned. And the shipped first_comment.txt that carries the line is read and asserted to carry it, so the defect is recorded as a reader received it rather than as a fixture describes it. Forced red by putting the old `kind` rule back: four cases fail, including the shipped 2026-08-30 aggregates, and restoring the predicate turns them green.
upgrades.the_cost_taken_deliberately: runs/carousel/2026-08-21 really did compute 481 days and declared it only in a `computed_by` sentence, so this drops a TRUE line from a deck of that shape. Omitting a true provenance line is a smaller harm than publishing a false one, and the cure is one field pair rather than a parser for English. Written into the function's docstring rather than left to be rediscovered.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: A deck that genuinely computes a day count and declares its two dates still comes out without the line, which would mean the field names drifted and the predicate is reading keys nothing writes. The shipped-aggregate half of the self-test is what carries that, because it asserts the line is EARNED on two dates as well as withheld on two.

upgrades.what: `claims_check` sweeps every prose snapshot in the run's own `sources/` for the deck's subject nouns and warns on any provision that names one and holds no claim's quote and is named nowhere in `rejected` or `notes`.
upgrades.why: Deck no. 18's thesis was refuted by Section 2-19-9 of an ordinance the run had fetched in full, cited six other sections of, and never opened. The ordinance names artificial intelligence in twelve places across five provisions and the run had read one. A second one the same run, the same shape: the council's Actions Taken By Council page was linked from an agenda the run had already fetched, and the run's rejected list said the agenda publishes no vote, which was true of the page's prose and skipped the link sitting on it. Both were found by a scoring judge. THE WHOLE PIPELINE IS ORIENTED ONE WAY. claims_check, aggregate_check, numeral_trace, noun_trace, locator_trace and absence_check all ask whether what the deck PRINTS traces back to a source. Not one asked whether what a SOURCE says came forward. This runs at Phase 6, before a frame exists, which is the last moment the answer is cheap.
upgrades.nothing_in_it_is_typed_but_the_stopwords: A SUBJECT TERM is a maximal run of two or more content words in the run's own `story` sentence that also appears in at least one claim's `text`. Maximal runs need no window length and no frequency floor, so there is no number to tune and none to creep. On 2026-09-08 that yields exactly `artificial intelligence` and `city manager`, and drops `austin ordered security equipment` and `same resolution forbade`, which no claim states in those words. A PROVISION is the span from one section heading to the next, and a document with no section headings is one provision, which makes this SILENT on an unsectioned source. That boundary is stated where the checker is defined rather than left to be inferred, which is GATE_LESSONS entry 49 ("The gate enforced ten rules and could observe four").
upgrades.verification: Fourteen new self-test cases. The synthetic half fixes what a subject term is, what it is not, and that a section id cited inside a sentence opens no provision. The real artifact half is the replay: the committed runs/carousel/2026-09-08/sources/ordinance.txt, the claims file as it ships, and the same file with every claim quoting inside 2-19-9 taken back out of it. As shipped, nothing is reported against the deck's subject noun. With 2-19-9 removed, the sweep NAMES 2-19-9, which is the section that refuted the thesis. The removal is asserted to have changed the file, so an empty result cannot pass as a clean one, which is GATE_LESSONS entry 63 ("Three self-tests passed on a fixture the code never saw"). Writing that section into `rejected` quiets it, which is the explicitly-reject arm of the judge's own rule and not a way to switch the gate off. Calibrated at two findings or fewer on the shipped deck, recorded as a number the way absence_check records its warning ceilings. Run live against out/2026-09-08 it prints one warning, the three ordinance provisions naming the city manager that no claim quotes, and exit stays 0.
upgrades.warn_never_fail: The same reason absence_check and noun_trace give. Deciding that a provision did not matter is an editorial judgement, and a gate that hard-fails a correct decision is a gate somebody switches off. What this does is put the list in front of the run while a rebuild still costs nothing. It also prints what it swept on the clean path as well as the dirty one, because a sweep that found no snapshots and a sweep that found nothing wrong must not print the same line.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: The subject term list comes back empty or comes back with five entries on a normal deck. Empty means the story sentence and the claim texts no longer share wording, and the gate has gone silent without saying so, which the printed term list is there to make visible on every run. Five entries means it has become a wolf-crier and the run learns to scroll past it, and the calibration case in the self-test is what turns that into a red rather than a feeling.

frontier_scan.focus: verification that a model READ what it fetched, rather than that what it wrote traces back
frontier_scan.why_this_focus: chosen from the run rather than from a rotation table, because both of the day's largest defects were the same omission and this repository has no vocabulary for it
frontier_scan.finding: The failure has a name and a measurement in the retrieval evaluation literature, and this project had neither. Work on RAG evaluation classifies a statement supported by a retrieved passage and not carried into the answer as SUPPORTED BUT MISSED, separately from unsupported, and treats recall as the first metric to watch when omission rather than fabrication is the risk. Legal-domain work on citation grounding reports leading systems producing false or incomplete provision citations at rates in the tens of percent and identifies exactly this class, an exception or prohibition in a fetched instrument that never reaches the answer. Completeness checking against a regulation is posed there as classifying text spans against provisions, which is the same unit the sweep above chose independently.
frontier_scan.what_was_taken_from_it: The unit. Occurrence-level counting produced twenty three findings for one term on one document and was unusable; provision-level counting produced two lines a run can act on. That framing came from the completeness-checking work rather than from this repository.
frontier_scan.what_was_refused: Everything model-based. The published methods score groundedness with a judge model, which is a number produced by a language model about a language model's output, and the compute-not-generate law forbids exactly that. The sweep is a substring search over a snapshot, and its answer is reproducible from the same files by anyone.

gate_lessons_draft.note: knowledge/shared/GATE_LESSONS.md is `human` lane and the upgrade lane may not write it. Draft text for a maintainer, one entry per upgrade above.
gate_lessons_draft.entry_for_the_value_arc: A gate that reads one form of a declaration sleeps on the second. check_value_arc knew two shapes for a planned value arc, a fenced F1 24 block and an inline comma list, and both were taken off real storyboards. Carousel 22 wrote its plan a third way, once per frame inside each dossier's own value_structure, which is the key the dossier spec asks for the value structure in. Nine declarations, and the gate printed `this storyboard declares no value arc this gate can read` and passed a deck whose median landed 14.5 L* below its own plan, with four of nine frames inside half a point of each other at the floor. The third-state detector added three days earlier for exactly this class could not see it either, because it only looks INSIDE a span that names the value arc and this file had no such span: a guard scoped to the thing it is guarding cannot see a miss that happens outside it. What to check instead: when a gate reads a declaration out of prose, ask where the writer would most naturally put it. The spec's own format block is the answer, and the form belongs written down in the spec so the writer and the checker are reading one sentence.
gate_lessons_draft.entry_for_the_round_counter: A counter of invocations is not a counter of the thing. panel.py's round counter returned the length of its own log, so every call to the combiner was a round. Carousel 22 re-ran the combiner once against a stale judge card while correcting a round's bookkeeping, the counter read 6 where five panels had sat, and the run wrote a prose correction into score.json beside the number. The cap that number feeds ships a deck UNDER the bar, so one high is one round nearer shipping something nobody scored. What to check instead: count the evidence, not the calls. A round is three judge cards this counter has not seen, identified by a digest of their content rather than by a filename or an mtime, both of which the run chooses.

frontier_scan.focus: verifying that a rendered scene contains the objects its plan declared. Rotated to the defect this run paid three scoring rounds for.
frontier_scan.kept: SceneCritic (arXiv 2604.13035) evaluates generated 3D layouts SYMBOLICALLY, over the layout program rather than the render, and two of its three constraint objectives are whether all required objects are placed and whether each object's bounding box lies inside the spatial boundary. That is the assertion built here, arrived at independently and confirmed. Graphics has a name for the test and a convention for it: view-frustum culling, which is done against an object's BOUNDING VOLUME and never its centre point, which is why this gate tests a body box rather than a projected point.
frontier_scan.kept_second: The web testing literature states this run's defect in one sentence. 'A functional test asserts on the DOM, not rendered output. A checkout button that has moved behind the footer still exists in the DOM and fires its click handler, so every functional assertion passes while no user can reach it.' Every gate in this suite is the functional assertion in that sentence.
frontier_scan.refused: A vision model asked whether the figure is in the picture. CI installs pyyaml and nothing else, GATE_LESSONS 15 is the entry about a gate that passed fifteen times locally and failed on the first push for exactly that, and a verdict that moves when a model moves is not a verdict a project whose whole argument is recomputability can publish. The small-object detection literature says the same thing from the other side.
frontier_scan.filed: The requirements-engineering literature calls the band half by its right name, auditing a specification for criteria that cannot be satisfied, and it puts the check at WRITING time rather than after the render. That is the better version and it is in the backlog with the arithmetic.

upgrades.what: scripts/carousel/bleed_witness.py, a new gate that reads every drawn box out of each slide's own script and fails when a declared bleed is not made by any of them.
upgrades.why: Carousel no. 27's frames 4, 5 and 7 end 152, 250 and 148 px above the bottom edge while declaring a bottom bleed, and frame 2's declared top bleed is a hard edge at y 392 with left and right undeclared. The harm is mechanical: `ROTATION['min_bleed_frames']` requires four bleeding frames on a deck and counts them off the declarations, so a deck can satisfy the image law on paper and draw no bleed at all. This one came within one frame of doing it.
upgrades.why_the_source_and_not_the_pixels: The bottom row of frame 4 is a drawn reading table, so a pixel reading of that edge says something is drawn there and is correct. The claim under test is narrower, that THE PRIMARY IMAGE runs off the edge, and no detector recovers which drawn thing is the subject from a rendered frame. `scene_bounds.py` established the source route on this repo's own slides and this gate imports its readers rather than writing a second copy.
upgrades.the_asymmetry_that_is_the_whole_design: REACHES an edge (x <= 0, x + w >= W) is the same predicate `layout_check` applies to the declared rect, and it is what WITNESSES a bleed. CROSSES an edge, strictly past it, is what makes a frame checkable at all: a box drawn past an edge proves the frame composes its image in coordinates that run off the canvas, so the absence of a box at another edge is evidence. A box stopping exactly on an edge proves nothing either way. Five of nine frames on this deck compose with a projected scene and are reported UNRESOLVED by name, and the count of frames actually checked is printed on success as well as on failure.
upgrades.no_threshold_was_typed: There is none to type. Both predicates are comparisons against the frame's own 1080 by 1350 bounds, and `layout_check` already owns that pair.
upgrades.the_three_false_positives_it_produced_fi: Run over all 27 shipped decks before it was wired to anything, the first cut reported carousels 22, 24 and 25 as missing a declared bleed by 1078.75, 1079.70 and 1348.48 px. The engine draws scenes in METRES, so a 2.50 m gantry part and a 0.60 m desk screen parse as boxes two pixels across sitting off the left edge. Three structural guards followed, each with a self-test case kept verbatim from the deck that produced it: an object literal inside an ARRAY is a part of a model and not a placement, a call carrying `X` or `Z` at the top level of an argument is a scene call in metres (names copied from assets/js/txscene.js, with a self-test asserting the copy still holds), and a box under one unit in either dimension is not a box in a space whose quantum is the pixel.
upgrades.verification: `bleed_witness.py --self-test` replays carousel no. 27's own numbers in both directions: the shipped sheet at y 366 h 832 FAILS its declared bottom bleed naming 152 px short, and the same declaration over a sheet drawn to 1350 passes, so only the geometry moved. It also asserts the two metre-space fixtures are not read as placements, that a commented-out call is not a drawing, that a nested object inside a content function is not the panel's geometry, that a projected-scene frame decides nothing and says why, that draw-time geometry is named rather than skipped, and that a run archiving no slide HTML exits 2 saying it CANNOT RUN. upgrades.wiring: `guards.yml` and `prompts/daily_routine.md` are `human` lane, so this lane's two routes are both taken: registered in `shipped_check.GATES` as CURRENT with `BLEED_SINCE = 2026-09-17`, which one guards.yml step runs against every published deck, and called by `panel_ready.check_bleed_witness` before the routine spawns a panel. `gate_wiring` grades 97 gates and reports every one run by something.

upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: A frame whose primary image bleeds one edge through a projected plane while also drawing a crossing box would be reported falsely. That is the one false positive this shape can produce, every finding names the call and the line it measured so the misreading is visible in the message, and the answer if it happens is to make the dossier describe the drawing rather than to widen the gate. If findings start arriving on frames whose declarations are honest, this gate is measuring the wrong object and should be narrowed to the box the dossier's own rect matches, not relaxed.

frontier_scan.focus: gates that cannot fail, and how the industry finds them. Timeboxed, four searches.
frontier_scan.kept: Mutation testing's discipline, not its tooling. A surviving mutant is a change to the code under test that no assertion noticed, and that is precisely what happened here three times: deleting SUBJECT_OF_NEGATION, deleting the prose glob, or hollowing the gazetteer each had to be shown to flip a result. So every check added today carries its mutant in a comment at the assertion, in the form 'delete X and this goes green', and each was run rather than asserted. The tautological-test literature names the same failure from the other end: a test whose expected value comes from the code it tests passes whatever the code does, which is GATE_LESSONS 16 in this repo's words.
frontier_scan.discarded: Running mutmut or cosmic-ray over this repo's gates in CI. These gates take run artifacts rather than pure arguments, so most mutants would be equivalent or uncompilable against a fixture, the runtime is minutes per gate against a suite already measured in tens of minutes, and the per-check hand mutant recorded above buys the part that matters at no CI cost. A tool that is too slow to run is a tool nobody runs, which is GATE_LESSONS 33's argument for one command.

2026-09-19 upgrade.run: carousel no. 29, the water reporting enforcement chain. Five scoring rounds, two hard fails, and a gate that was asymmetric for thirteen months
2026-09-19 upgrade.diagnosis: Three of the run's five scoring rounds repaired the CLASS at the INSTANCE a judge pointed at, and the round 4 integrity judge wrote the lesson as his one sentence fix: repair the class across all nine before re-scoring. Round 5 then found seven more siblings of a falsehood rounds 1 and 4 had each repaired once. Underneath that, three separate machine holes were measured and are not opinions. `sources_block.check()` asked one of the two questions a sources block has to answer, so round 1's repair went red correctly on a missing id and round 2's repair passed silently on an extra one, the same file, the same gate, mirror image, consecutive rounds. The crawl boundary lives in a `human` owned prose file and is re-implemented by every fetcher that needs it, so this run's own helper carried it as a tuple of HOSTS and fetched one `capitol.texas.gov/TLODOCS/` url, which is a disallowed PATH on an allowed host. And the vector PDF shipped at 61.8 MB against a 6 to 21.6 MB corpus with nothing in the suite measuring the file the owner has to upload.

upgrades.what: `sources_block.check()` asks both directions. A block listing a claim id that no frame and no caption prints is now a failure, and the message names WHICH direction, because the two cures are different files.
upgrades.why: The gate tested only that every id the DECK prints is in the BLOCK, so a superset passed. On 2026-09-19 round 1 moved frame 1 onto c4 and frame 5 off c17 and c21 without rebuilding the block, and the gate went red exactly as designed, found by a scoring judge rather than by the run. Round 2 then moved c14 off frame 8, the block went on listing c14, and `--check` exited 0. An integrity judge read the block against the nine footers and found it. An id in the block that is on no slide is a receipt for a purchase nobody made, and it is the only VISIBLE evidence of the larger fault underneath, which is that the block was not rebuilt after the deck moved.
upgrades.the_comparison_is_against_every_citing_s: Printed ids come from `copy.json` plus any id in `caption.txt`, never from the frames alone. No shipped caption carries one, measured across all 29 decks, which is exactly why the caption is read: a selector that can only see the surface it was written against is GATE_LESSONS 39, and this file has already been that entry once. `first_comment.txt` is excluded because it IS the block, and reading the thing under test as evidence for itself makes the comparison vacuous.
upgrades.six_shipped_decks_are_exempt_by_name_and: Measured before a line was written, over all 29 run directories, against `copy.json` AND against every claim id in each deck's own `render_report.json` text nodes, so none is a frame that printed an id the copy failed to record: 2026-08-25 c23; 2026-08-27 c4 c5 c12 c14 c16 c18 c19; 2026-08-28 c1 c11 c14 c16 c20 c21 c23 c25; 2026-09-03 c1 c15 c17; 2026-09-04 c5 c10 c11 c16 c17; 2026-09-09 c13. Those blocks were posted as comments under published decks, so rewriting the files would not reach a reader; it would only make a gate green about a comment that still says what it says. That is the identical argument the file already makes for `SHIPPED_BEFORE_THE_RULE`, and it is a SECOND constant rather than an addition to that one, because those runs did not predate the rule, they broke it. `email_check --all` runs this over every shipped deck in CI, so without the exemption the check could not have shipped at all.
upgrades.the_exemption_cannot_grow: The self-test asserts that the newest directory under `runs/carousel/` is in neither exemption set, so a run under scoring pressure that adds its own date to go green turns the suite red in the same commit. It also re-measures each exempt deck's artifacts and fails on an exemption that is no longer needed, so a stale line is a line to delete rather than a permanent carve-out nobody re-reads.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/sources_block.py --self-test`, which replays round 2's shape: the block is built while the deck prints c1..c4, a repair takes c4 off its frame, nothing rebuilds the block, and the check goes red naming c4 and the direction. The assertion beside it proves the OLD one-directional check exited 0 on that identical input. Watched red outside the suite too, on the real artifact: copying `runs/carousel/2026-09-19/` and inserting `c14` into its first comment gives exit 1 with the stale-block message, and removing it gives exit 0. `python3 scripts/carousel/email_check.py --all` is green over all 29 shipped decks.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: A run whose caption or first comment legitimately cites a claim in prose that no frame prints starts failing here. The caption is already read into the printed set; a comment body that cites outside the block would need the same treatment, and the tell is a finding naming an id the run knows it published somewhere a reader can see. If the fix for that is ever to delete the reverse check rather than widen the surface set, the check has been switched off rather than repaired.

upgrades.what: `scripts/shared/crawl_boundary.py`. One place that reads the crawl boundary out of `SOURCES_REGISTRY.md` and answers whether a url is refused, handling hosts and paths as two different kinds of rule.
upgrades.why: The registry states the boundary and is `human` owned, correctly, because an unattended run that can edit its own boundary does not have one. Nothing READ it, so every fetcher carried its own copy of the rule. This run's research helper carried it as a tuple of hosts and fetched one `capitol.texas.gov/TLODOCS/` url, which is a disallowed PATH on an allowed host and a tuple of hosts cannot express it. Nothing from the fetch reached a claim and the helper was repaired the same hour, and the helper is scratch under `out/`, so that repair died with the container and the next run writes the tuple again from memory.
upgrades.none_is_not_permission: `forbidden(url)` returns a reason or None, and None means only that no rule this parser could read matches. The registry is prose written for people, its boundary is stated in four table shapes and twice in running text, and a parser over prose is complete only until somebody writes the next row differently. The module docstring, the CLI's success line and the `--list` footer all say this in as many words, because the failure mode of a boundary checker is a caller reading silence as a yes.
upgrades.a_parse_that_finds_nothing_is_a_hard_fai: `rules()` raises rather than returning a short list. A parse that silently finds zero entries produces a checker that permits everything and exits 0, which is GATE_LESSONS 37. The floor is five, measured against the shipped registry on 2026-09-19, and the self-test pins each of the five hosts and each of the four disallowed capitol paths by name, so a reformat that drops one goes red in the suite instead of quietly widening the boundary.
upgrades.the_partial_parse_was_the_real_hazard: The first working draft read `/Search/` and `/Reports/` off the section 4 robots row and left `/BillLookup/` permitted, because the registry writes the first path glued to the host. A boundary checker that is wrong about ONE path is more dangerous than no checker, since the next fetcher trusts it. The host prefix is stripped now and all three are pinned in the self-test.
upgrades.two_readings_inherited_rather_than_inven: Case: `Disallow: /TLODOCS/` is upper case and the live urls are lower, and the registry says taking a case sensitive reading is routing around a disallow on a technicality. Matching is case folded. Subdomains: a whole host rule covers the names under it, which over-refuses rather than under-refuses, and that is the only direction a boundary may be wrong in. The verified substitute the registry names on the same host, `Committees/MeetingsUpcoming.aspx`, is asserted NOT refused, because a checker that sends a run away from the source the registry just recommended costs the run its story.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/shared/crawl_boundary.py --self-test`, which replays the 2026-09-19 fetch in both cases, pins the five host rules and the four capitol paths, asserts the verified substitute is not refused, and proves that a registry parsing to no boundary and a registry parsing to one rule both RAISE rather than returning an empty allow list. Watched red at the command line: `crawl_boundary.py https://capitol.texas.gov/TLODOCS/88R/HB1.pdf` exits 1 with the registry's own words.
upgrades.lane_note: `ownership.yaml` gives `scripts/shared/**` to `daily`, not to `upgrade`, and the parent instruction that this phase owns it was wrong about the map. The map's own carve-out note and the pre-commit hook's message both say a `claude/daily-` branch may stamp `daily` for a defect the run caused or is blocked by, and a disallowed fetch is exactly that. So this file ships in a commit of its own stamped `daily`, carrying nothing else, which keeps the property the lane split exists for: no commit from this phase both edits the machine and holds the daily lane over anything else.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: A fetcher starts treating a None answer as permission, which the self-test cannot catch and only reading the call site can. Or the registry gains a boundary row in a shape this parser does not read and the floor still passes at five, which is the partial parse again one size up. The mitigation is that the pinned list is per host and per path rather than a count, so a rule that moves has to move past a named assertion.
upgrades.revert: the daily-stamped commit that added scripts/shared/crawl_boundary.py

upgrades.what: `email_check` refuses a deck PDF over the size LinkedIn publishes as its document limit, and prints the newest run's size and headroom on every invocation, pass or fail.
upgrades.why: Carousel no. 29's vector PDF shipped at 61,765,403 bytes. All 28 decks before it sit between 6 and 21.6 MB and the median is near 10. Nothing in the suite measured it. `email_check` proves the PDF EXISTS and that the email LINKS it, which is two thirds of 'the owner can post this' and silently not the third, so a render decision is free to quadruple the file and the first thing to report it would be the upload failing in front of the one human this routine has.
upgrades.the_threshold_is_not_ours_and_cannot_cre: LinkedIn's own document-post help page says 'The file size cannot exceed 100MB and 300 pages'. That is the door the deck is posted through, it was published by somebody else for the surface the file actually goes to, and it is cited at the constant with the date it was read. A ceiling measured off our own decks would be a number this project typed, and re-deriving it from a corpus it had already tightened is the ratchet GATE_LESSONS names under 'The rule for setting a threshold'. MB is taken as 10^6 rather than 2^20, which is the reading that REFUSES MORE, because a gate that guesses the generous reading and is wrong fails at upload time, which is the failure it exists to prevent.
upgrades.it_would_not_have_failed_this_run_and_sa: 61.8 MB is 62 percent of the limit and postable. The self-test asserts exactly that: carousel no. 29 is reported postable AND is over three tenths of the allowance. What the change buys is the headroom line, printed on success as well as on failure, so a run walking towards the cliff is visible before it arrives rather than at it. That is `text_contrast.mjs`'s rule about printing what it declined, applied to a size.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/email_check.py --self-test`. A sparse `carousel.pdf` truncated to one byte over the limit is caught; truncated to exactly the limit it passes, because the platform's wording is CANNOT EXCEED. The limit constant is asserted to be LinkedIn's published figure rather than a corpus measurement, so an edit that replaces it with one of our own numbers goes red. `--all` over 29 shipped decks is green and prints '2026-09-19: carousel.pdf is 61.8 MB, 62% of the 100 MB LinkedIn states as its document limit'.
upgrades.how_i_would_know_this_was_wrong: LinkedIn changes the limit, or means 2^20 by MB and a deck between 95.4 and 100 MB is refused here and would have uploaded. Either way the fix is to re-read the help page and move the constant WITH its citation, never to derive a number from our own files. And if a deck ever fails this gate, the fix is the halftone and the grain rather than the threshold: this run measured about 5 MB in the screen cell and about 9 MB in grain and dither, with the residual being the full screen across all nine frames.
upgrades.revert: the commit that changed scripts/carousel/email_check.py on this branch

refused_and_why.a gate over claims.json's `rejected` arr: BUILT AS A PROTOTYPE, MEASURED, AND NOT SHIPPED, because the measurement says the naive form is worse than the defect. The backlog proposal was to rank each rejected finding against the published strings by content-word overlap and report the nearest. Replayed on this run it works beautifully in isolation: round 1's offending dek, 'The request goes to developers of data centers 25 MW and larger.', scores 0.80 against the rejection 'That the request goes to EVERY data center developer of 25 MW and larger', with the next nearest shipped string at 0.30. Then the same measurement over all 29 shipped decks gives a per-deck maximum of 0.33 to 0.86, median near 0.55. A deck legitimately talks about the subject its own rejections are about, so 0.80 is indistinguishable from the corpus background and the score carries no signal. Shipping it would have been a row that is always amber, which GATE_LESSONS says is ignored exactly as fast as one that is always green. The honest form needs the optional machine-readable `forbids` field the backlog asked for, and that field has to be written by the fact checker, which is `prompts/daily_routine.md` and `human` lane. Filed with the numbers so the next phase starts from evidence rather than from the hunch this one started from.
refused_and_why.an instrument-repeat dimension in dedupe: Refused on measurement, again. The ledger's angle_note has now asked for this five times in capitals and this deck is the fifth ERCOT request in the window. `dedupe_check` already reads the hosts out of every deck's committed claims file and its own docstring already states the limit that bites here: two ERCOT decks can read a board presentation and a market notice, which are different instruments at one host. Two mechanical routes were measured today and both are empty. No two decks in the window cite a single identical source URL, so an exact-document comparison finds nothing. And tokenising every deck's document TITLES across the window, the only words shared by four or more decks are 'texas' and 'meeting', so a title comparison would not have named this repeat either. What is left is classifying a document by KIND, which is a vocabulary problem and the recognition problem this backlog has already refused a gate for twice.
refused_and_why.a third upgrade for its own sake: Three is the ceiling and not the target. Two of the three that shipped came out of the backlog with their cautions already written; the third came from a measurement nobody had made. The two refusals above are each worth more as a table of numbers in the backlog than as a gate shipped without calibration, and this file is append only, so what gets logged is permanent.

frontier_scan.focus: Rotated to the largest lever the panel named: deriving a dossier's named parts from what the chassis actually DREW, instead of comparing prose to prose. Ten searches, one finding worth acting on and one route refused.
frontier_scan.the_finding: The tractable mechanism is not segmentation and it is not a model. It is instrumenting the 2D context. `canvas-interceptor` patches `CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype` and logs every method call and its arguments to a property on the context; `jest-canvas-mock` does the same and exposes a `_drawCall` list per operation; DataDome's canvas work records `fillRect` and its arguments with the caller's source url and line. All three are dependency free ES5 or ES6 in the page. Applied here it would give the render report a list of the primitives each frame actually drew, at their actual coordinates, which is the declarative shape list `scene_bounds` and `bleed_witness` get for free from SVG and that this project's canvas frames have never had.
frontier_scan.why_it_matters_here: The 2026-09-18 phase tried twice to recover 'the largest non-background shape' by segmenting pixels and both routes ranked the wrong frames, because every drawn thing touches something else and the largest component is the frame. A draw-call log sidesteps the recognition problem entirely: a dossier that names a lit west gable, a dark return and a gap of lit sky can be held against the primitives that exist, and the four frames this run gave 40 to 55 percent of the canvas to empty graded ground would be arithmetic rather than a judgement.
frontier_scan.refused: A vision model reading the frame and answering whether the declared part is present. Same refusal as 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-04 and for the same two reasons: CI installs pyyaml and nothing else, which is GATE_LESSONS 15, and a verdict that moves when a model moves is not a verdict a project whose whole argument is recomputability gets to publish.
frontier_scan.why_it_is_a_proposal_and_not_a_change: The injection point is the render harness, `.claude/skills/carousel-engine/render.py`. `ownership.yaml` gives that path to `upgrade` and the host treats every path under `.claude/` as a sensitive file and prompts on any edit whatever the permission mode says. Ownership and reachability are different questions and the map answers only the first.

proposals_out_of_lane.what: Instrument `CanvasRenderingContext2D` in the render harness and emit the draw-call log into `render_report.json`, then check each dossier's named parts against the primitives that exist. Prototype-patch the context before the frame's script runs, record method name, arguments and the current transform, and cap the log per frame. No dependency, no model, and it is the mechanism the round 5 integrity judge asked for in his one sentence fix.
proposals_out_of_lane.why: The plan is prose and the frame is code, and nothing checks that they describe the same picture. `plan_render_check` compares declared STRINGS, claim sets, palette tokens and library names, and every one of those can be satisfied by a frame that draws none of the objects the dossier names.

proposals_out_of_lane.what: `render.py` collects `window.__akLeaders`, a sibling project's prefix, while every Texas frame sets `window.__txLeaders`. One word.
proposals_out_of_lane.why: Measured again on this run's `render_report.json`: `leaders`, `rules`, `contacts`, `encodings`, `svg_plates` and `canvas_text` are `[]` on all nine slides. The declarative half of every acceptance list this repo writes has still never been machine-checked, and it is the precondition for the proposal above. Filed by the 2026-09-18 phase and unchanged.

proposals_out_of_lane.why: The fact checker already writes the refusal and the permitted wording in prose. Nothing in `scripts/carousel/` can act on it, and the overlap measurement above shows no purely mechanical route to the same answer. The gate is one lane and the field is another.

red_gates_repaired_under_the_failure_pro.why_this_is_not_a_fourth_upgrade: CI went red on `shipped_check.py`, which is this lane's file, and CLAUDE.md's rule is that red is work now. Both findings are repairs to a gate that was already there rather than new capability, and each carries the self-test case that proves it can still go red. The upgrade count stands at three.
red_gates_repaired_under_the_failure_pro.g_shipped_fresh_compared_display_copy_ag: The gate flattened tags and collapsed whitespace and left the literal ` ` standing in the text, so frame 3's letterhead, `OFFICE OF THE TEXAS GOVERNOR   SEPTEMBER 14TH, 2026`, could not match the one-space string `copy.json` records. **CI was red on a correct artifact**, which is the most expensive shape a gate failure takes, because the obvious cure is to put markup into the copy record and that would make the record describe the HTML rather than the page. The gate's own docstring says its subject is every display string `copy.json` records, and a display string is what the browser renders. `html.unescape` goes between the two substitutions: AFTER the tag strip, because unescaping first would turn an escaped `<section>` in visible copy into a tag and delete it, and BEFORE the whitespace collapse, because U+00A0 is matched by `\s` in str mode. Three self-test cases: the real letterhead is found; a string the frame does NOT carry still fails with the same entity in the same place, so the decode cannot become a way to pass; and an escaped angle bracket a frame displays is not eaten as a tag.
red_gates_repaired_under_the_failure_pro.crawl_boundary_was_run_by_nothing: `gate_wiring` reported it the moment it existed, which is that check doing exactly its job. The three routes it accepts are a workflow, a routine phase and `shipped_check`'s registry, and the first two are `human` lane, so the registry is the only one this actor can reach. The adapter is not an import for its own sake: it asks whether any claim a shipped deck stands on cites a url inside the crawl boundary, which is a question about published work that nothing else in the suite could answer, since `claims_check` proves a claim is fetched and quoted and has no opinion about where from.
red_gates_repaired_under_the_failure_pro.and_it_found_three_decks: Measured over every shipped deck: 2026-08-16 cites `lrl.texas.gov` on c28, c29 and c31 and 2026-08-21 cites it on c3 through c8, both BEFORE that host was decided off limits on August 25th. 2026-09-07 cites `docs.tacc.utexas.edu` on eighteen claims, which is a SUBDOMAIN of the host the registry names, and whether a domain-wide statement reaches a subdomain with its own robots.txt is a question for the maintainer who owns that file. frontier_scan.focus: Rotated to the question the refused chassis gate raises: measuring a composite instead of reading a constant. Eight searches, one finding worth acting on, and it subsumes three separate open backlog items.
frontier_scan.the_finding: The accessibility literature settled this years ago for text over photographs and the rule it reached is the one this repo needs. Contrast is measured PER PIXEL against the worst-case ground under any character of the text, using the WCAG relative luminance `L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B` and the ratio `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)`. The guidance says plainly that automated tools cannot answer it from source and that the rendered pixel has to be sampled, which is GATE_LESSONS 1 arriving from outside this project. Canvas testing practice adds the mechanical half: sample the BACKING STORE and assert RGBA there, separately from the composite screenshot, because erasing on a transparent canvas reduces alpha rather than painting a colour. The effective-opacity formula `1 - (1 - a)^n` for n overlapping layers is standard and is exactly the arithmetic that produced this run's 0.783.
frontier_scan.what_it_makes_possible: If the render harness emitted an ART-ONLY pass per frame, the same draw with the type layer hidden, ONE gate reading the line boxes `render_report.json` already records could answer three open items at once: whether a wash behind type composites past its ceiling, asked of the pixel rather than of the source and therefore immune to being drawn in a loop in canvas; whether the wash LIFTS where the art is already darker than the ground, which is the sign error the round 5 craft judge named twice and which is still unfixed; and whether the type clears a contrast floor an EXTERNAL standard sets. WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 are external, so nothing there is derived from our own corpus and nothing there can ratchet.
frontier_scan.why_it_cannot_be_built_here: A gate measuring the SHIPPED png would be reading the glyphs themselves rather than the ground under them, because the shipped png already has the type painted on it. The art-only pass is `.claude/skills/carousel-engine/render.py`, which `ownership.yaml` gives to `upgrade` and the host makes unreachable to an unattended run.

proposals_out_of_lane.what: Emit an ART-ONLY render pass per frame, the same draw with the type layer hidden, beside `render_report.json`. Then `scripts/carousel/` can measure the worst-case ground luminance under every line box the report already records and hold it against the glyph colour, per the WCAG per-pixel rule. One measurement replaces `deck_chassis.PLATE_ALPHA`'s source proxy, catches a canvas wash drawn in a loop that the CSS parser can never see, and catches a wash that lifts where the art is darker than the ground.
proposals_out_of_lane.why: `PLATE_ALPHA` reads a constant in CSS source. This run's chassis breached it by forty two percent in canvas, measured at 0.783 against 0.55 across eleven line boxes, and every round was green. The static detector for it was prototyped this phase and reports the same four findings on the broken and the repaired chassis, so source analysis is closed. The pixel is the only instrument left and the art-only pass is the only thing missing.

2026-09-21.diagnosis: Two of this run's three faults are the same shape and it is the shape this backlog keeps finding. A MODULE HELD A NUMBER, OR A FILE, THAT ONLY ONE PATH EVER MAINTAINED, AND EVERY OTHER PATH LEFT IT QUIETLY WRONG. `panel.py` derives its round count from a log it appends to, and rounds 1 to 3 were scored by agents that never invoked it, so a deck at its five round cap carried `rounds: 2` and told the run to keep working. `ship_images.py` deletes a source PNG after a verified encode and nothing said only one of it may run, so two launched at once raced and slide 02 shipped with no image at all. The third is the run's charged defect and is not that shape: sixteen declared-but-absent elements across four scoring rounds, because a per frame acceptance list asserts measurable properties and nothing in the suite measures them.

upgrades.what: `panel.py` writes the round the panel actually ran. `rounds` is now the larger of what this module's log has seen and what three distinct judge cards from three distinct lenses agree they are, the verdict carries `rounds_derived`, `rounds_declared`, `rounds_source` and `at_cap` beside it, and a HOLD at the cap says AT CAP rather than 'Keep working the deck'.
upgrades.why: Three cards each stamped `"round": 5` combined to `"rounds": 2`. That is not cosmetic and it suppressed the run's whole public output. `run_complete.check`'s cap path is the only one that licenses a deck under the bar with no hard fail, it is reachable only at `rounds >= max_rounds`, and three surfaces read it. `shipped_check`'s completion gate was red. `site_context.load_runs` delegates publication to the same call, so `docs/articles/2026-09-21/` was never built. `article_check` reported 30 editions on a day that should have 31. An independent reviewer on the pull request filed the same path as a P1 from the other direction.
upgrades.why_the_cards_and_not_the_log: THE TWO WITNESSES FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THAT IS WHAT DECIDES IT. `panel_rounds.jsonl` can only UNDERCOUNT, because it records what happened to be routed through one function and a round it never saw is a round it cannot hold. A card can only OVERCOUNT, because a number on it is a number somebody could have typed. So the larger is the honest figure whenever the smaller one is a log. This does open a door `count_round`'s docstring spent a run closing, and the door is narrowed rather than left ajar. `believable_declared` refuses a declared round unless it is three cards, three distinct lenses and three distinct digests, which is every cheap way to manufacture one. A run that wants the cap this way has to have actually spawned the panel.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/panel.py --self-test`, which replays the real 2026-09-21 cards and the real derived count of 2. It asserts `rounds` is 5, `rounds_derived` is 2, the HOLD says AT CAP and does not say keep working, and then LOADS `run_complete` and asserts it says THE DECK DID NOT SHIP at rounds 2 and stops saying it at rounds 5, which is the gate that was red. The anti-gaming half asserts that two cards, three cards from one lens, three identical cards and a card set that disagrees with itself all buy nothing and leave `rounds` on the log's number. Replayed on the real artifact, `panel.py --date 2026-09-21 --judges runs/carousel/2026-09-21/scores/*.json` writes `rounds: 5` and `run_complete.check` on that verdict returns an empty list.

Every round's median is written into the run record, so the check is reading five numbers. If that ever happens the answer is not to distrust the cards again, it is that Phase 15 must route every scoring round through this module, after which the log is the larger number and none of this is reached.

upgrades.what: `ship_images.py` takes a per run lock before it mutates anything, and a second concurrent shipper raises `Busy` and exits 2 instead of racing. The lock is written whole and linked into place atomically, it records the holder's pid AND its process start time, a lock whose holder is not that live instance is taken over with a line saying so, and release unlinks only a lock that still names this process.
upgrades.why: This run launched two `ship_images.py` processes against one directory, one backgrounded with `&` and one with the tool's own background flag. The tool removes the source PNG after a verified encode, so the two raced over the only copy of each image and slide 02 came out with no image at all. Nothing reported it. The run found it by auditing the directory afterwards, and then froze rather than repairing it, which is the more serious half and is already a rule in CLAUDE.md.
upgrades.the_trap_this_avoids: `UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md` states it in as many words on the `guards_local --verdict` proposal. A guard a contributor has to clear by hand is a guard they learn to delete. So a stale lock never wedges a run. A pid alone is not an identity, because pids are recycled and a recycled number reads as a live holder, so the lock carries the kernel's own start time for that pid out of /proc field 22 and judges staleness on the instance.
upgrades.found_by_its_own_self_test: The first version used `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` then wrote the payload, which is two steps, and the concurrency case caught the window between them on its first run. The second shipper opened the empty file, read no pid, concluded the holder was dead and took the lock over. A lock with a race in it is worse than none, because it reads as a guarantee. It is `os.link` from a fully written staging file now.
upgrades.verification: `python3 scripts/carousel/ship_images.py --self-test`. Two threads call `ship()` on one directory and exactly one is refused while every slide keeps exactly one shipping image, which is the outcome this run lost. Beside it, a lock held by a reaped pid is taken over, a live pid with a disagreeing start time is read as a recycled number, a shipper releases only the lock it still holds, a lock is released when the body raises, and a dry run is never refused because it mutates nothing.
upgrades.seen_red: With the lock regressed to a no-op the concurrency assertion reports `a second shipper on one run is REFUSED  it was let in` and the suite exits non-zero. With the release guard removed, `a shipper releases only the lock it still holds` goes red. Run six times to check it is not flaky.

frontier_scan.worth_acting_on_and_acted_on: A pid is not an identity. The literature on pidfile locking is unanimous that judging staleness on pid existence alone is wrong under pid reuse, and that the cheap fix is to record the holder's process INSTANCE, which on Linux is the start time in field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat. The second finding is the release rule. A holder evicted as stale that then unlinks on its way out deletes the NEW holder's lock, so release must re-read and unlink only its own. Both are in the lock and both have a self-test case.
frontier_scan.worth_knowing_and_stated_as_a_limit: WCAG's own understanding of 1.4.11 says it is the KEY PARTS of a graphical object that must pass rather than every part, which is the argument for sampling two declared faces rather than the whole object. And the shape-from-shading literature is clear that the perceptual quantity is the shading GRADIENT rather than a step in luminance, and that the visual system assumes a single light from above. So a contrast ratio between two rects is a PROXY for whether an object turns in space. It is a good one for the failure this gate exists for, which is an object drawn with no faces at all, and it would not tell a well graded solid from a flat one lit from the wrong side.
frontier_scan.refused_again: Nothing model-shaped. CI installs pyyaml and a verdict that moves when a model moves is not a verdict this project can publish. GATE_LESSONS 15, and the 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-04 scans reached it first.

proposals_out_of_lane.what: A GATE_LESSONS entry for the two-witness rule, drafted here so a maintainer pastes rather than reconstructs. A COUNT AND A LOG CAN BOTH BE HONEST AND DISAGREE, AND WHICH ONE IS RIGHT IS DECIDED BY WHICH DIRECTION EACH CAN FAIL IN. `panel.py` derived a round count from a log it appends to and reported 2 for a deck whose three judge cards each said round 5. The log was honestly computed and three short, because rounds 1 to 3 were scored by agents that never invoked the module, and a log can only ever undercount a round it did not see. A card can only ever overcount. So the larger is the honest figure whenever the smaller is a log, and the cost of getting it wrong was not a red gate. `run_complete.check`'s cap path reads that number, `site_context.load_runs` delegates publication to the same call, and the day's edition was silently never built. WHAT TO CHECK INSTEAD. Where two surfaces carry the same fact, ask which way each can be wrong before deciding which to believe, and put BOTH in the artifact so a reader can see the derivation. And where the believed one is writable by the party being measured, make it pay. Three distinct cards from three distinct lenses is what a round costs here, which refuses every cheap forgery without refusing the real thing.

proposals_out_of_lane.what: A GATE_LESSONS entry for the mixed-format read, drafted. A FALLBACK WRITTEN AS `A or B` IS NOT A FALLBACK, IT IS A PRIORITY, AND THE DAY BOTH ARE PRESENT IT SILENTLY DROPS B. Two carousel gates resolved a deck's frames as `glob(png) or glob(webp)` with a comment describing it as reading whichever is there. Carousel 31 was the first deck to ship SOME frames as png and some as webp, because the encoder keeps the png wherever webp misses its quality floor, and both gates then measured seven of nine frames. One reported two frames missing. The other divided by seven and reported a confident ratio. A count that loses its subject reports a smaller number and a RATIO that loses its subject reports a wrong one, which is the more dangerous of the two and the one with no symptom. WHAT TO CHECK INSTEAD. Where a resolver has a preference, merge the candidates and key them on the thing that identifies one subject, then apply the preference per subject. And ask of any `or` between two globs how long it has been true that only one side is ever non-empty, because that is an assumption about the data rather than about the code and nothing announces the day it stops holding.
